segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Alright, let’s start.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Ok.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: First, I want your English names, Jerry.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎠᏯᏛ ᏓᏩᏙᎥ Jerry Scott-ᏙᏭ ᎮᎾ ᎯᎠᎾ Mary Cochran ᏄᎵᏍᏔᏅ *maiden name* Scott ᏃᏭ ᎺᎵᏭ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ ᏍᎩᏭᏍ ᎠᏯᏅ ᏩᎴᎳᏂᏓ ᏓᏩᏙᎠ
segments.transliteration: vv ayadv dawadov Jerry Scott-dowu hena hiana Mary Cochran nulistanv *maiden name* Scott nowu meliwu tsalagi gvdi sgiwus ayanv walelanida dawadoa
segments.translation: I’m Jerry Scott and this is Mary Cochran—used to be—maiden name. Scott now. Her name in Cherokee is Mel(i) and my name is Walenid(a).

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Walenid(a).

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏳᏍᏗ ᎦᏓᎧ ᏩᎴᎳᏂᏓ ᎠᏂᏓ ᏩᎴᎵ ᏩᎴᎳᏂᏓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏯᎦᏎᏍᏔᏅ ᎩᎶ ᎮᎾ ᏣᎩᏃᏎᎸ ᏧᏂᏍᏗ Hummingbird ᏩᎴ-Ꮹ-ᏩᎴᎳᏂᏓ ᎠᏂᏩᎴᎳᏂᏓ ᏣᎾᏔᏍ ᎠᏂᏓ ᎮᎾ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ uh...ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎮᎾ Hummingbirds ᎣᏍᏓ ᏣᏩᏓᏛᏁ Hummingbirds ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: yusdi gadaka walelanida anida waleli walelanida osda yagasestanv gilo hena tsaginoselv tsunisdi Hummingbird wale-wa-walelanida aniwalelanida tsanatas anida hena sginana uh...sginana hena Hummingbirds osda tsawadadvne Hummingbirds squu
segments.translation: The meaning of Walenid(a) it’s a little Walel(i). But if you listen, somebody told me it means a little hummingbird. Walenid(a), do you know it means ‘baby?’ They’re hummingbirds. And we are kin to the Hummingbirds.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is your name Mary?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mm-hmm. Mel(i) in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Mel(i) in Cherokee. Where were you born, Jerry?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Tahlequah. Are you asking where I was really born?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏓᎵᏆᏛ Ꮎ ᎠᏭᏴ ᎥᎾ ᎤᏪᏘ ᏥᎪᏢᏒ Ꮎ Hasting-Ꭲ
segments.transliteration: daliquadv na awuyv vna uweti tsigotlvsv na Hasting-i
segments.translation: Yeah, it was Tahlequah, where the old Hastings hospital was.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And you, Mary?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Uh-uh. I was born at my grandma’s house.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Oh. ᎢᎾᎨᎮ ᏣᏂᏁᎸ? ᏥᎾᏂᏪᏍᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎩᎶ ᏯᏛᏗ... “ᎢᎾᎨᏛ ᎠᏥᏂᏴᎲ,” ᏯᎾᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ... ᎥᎾᏭᏍ---ᎭᏢ ᏣᏛ.Ꮢ ᏂᎯ Jerry?
segments.transliteration: Oh. inagehe tsaninelv? tsinaniwesgo tsigehv gilo yadvdi... “inagedv atsiniyvhv,” yanada tsigehv ... vnawus---hatlv tsadv.sv nihi Jerry?
segments.translation: Oh. And they lived out in the woods? “In the woods,” that’s what they used to say. “He caught her in the woods,” they would say. Where did you grow up, Jerry?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Rocky Mt.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Rocky Mt.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Nvyodalv… Nvyodalv, that’s what they call it in Cherokee.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ‘ᏙᏅ ᎤᏍᏛ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏙᏓᎸ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏅᏲᏓᎸ ᏣᏓ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎨᎮ ᏙᏳ ᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: ‘donv usdv sgina tsidodalv ‘do usdi nvyodalv tsada ‘do usdi gehe doyu gehe?
segments.translation: Which one is it, of all the mountains, which one is the real Nvyodalv?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: It’s where the school is, they call it Nvyodalv.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎨᎢ Ᏹ--ᏱᏕᏣᎧᏅᏅ ᎥᎾ ᏗᏢ *south* ᏗᏢ ᏱᏕᏣᎧᏅᏅ ᏗᎦᏚᏏ ᏧᏍᏗ ᎥᎾᏴ ᏦᎦᏁᎵᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ *hooky* ᏃᎦᏛᏁᎸ ᏍᎩ ᎥᎾ ᏬᏥᏴᎲ *cave*-Ꭲ ᎤᏙᏓᏩᏓ ᏃᏭ *bus* ᏳᎶᏒ ᏃᏭ ᏫᎣᏥᎷᎬ ᏙᏣᎵᏍᎪᏁᎲ Ꮎ ᏦᎩᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏙᏣᏕᎶᏆᏨ ᎮᎾ ᏃᏭ ᎥᎾᏴ ᏦᏥᏯ ᏬᎦᏕᎩᏙᎲ Ꮭ ᏙᏳ, ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ ᎤᎪᏓ ᎨᎲ ᏗᏩᏕᎶᏆᎥ ᎮᎾ Ᏺ’
segments.transliteration: gei yi--yidetsakanvnv vna ditlv *south* ditlv yidetsakanvnv digadusi tsusdi vnayv tsoganelidi tsigehv *hooky* nogadvnelv sgi vna wotsiyvhv *cave*-i udodawada nowu *bus* yulosv nowu wiotsilugv dotsalisgonehv na tsogigayvlige dotsadeloquatsv hena nowu vnayv tsotsiya wogadegidohv tla doyu, nigohilv doyu hena ugoda gehv diwadeloquav hena yo’
segments.translation: When you look toward the south you can see the hills—that’s where we used to play. When we played hooky from school. That’s where we were, in a cave all day. And, when the bus would go by, then we would go home, in the evening. We would lie to our parents. We’d tell them that we’d been in school. We were out riding around, but not all the time. But I went to school a lot.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ Cave Springs ᏫᏕᎦᏓ--ᎥᎾᏍ ᏣᏕᎶᏆᎡ ᎨᎲ Cave Springs?
segments.transliteration: ayadv Cave Springs widegada--vnas tsadeloquae gehv Cave Springs?
segments.translation: I went to school at Cave Springs is that where you went to school too?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yes, Cave Springs.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I remember you there.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yeah, Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᎮᎾ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦᏓ ᏍᎩᏍᏊ ᏥᏃᎦᏛᏁᎴ ᎾᏛ *hooky* ᏥᏃᎦᏛᏁᎴ Ꮎ ᏧᏪᏴ ᎥᎾᏛ ᏌᏊ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᎢᏡᎬ ᎠᎹᏯ ᎦᏚ ᎥᎾ ᏦᎩᎴ ᏃᏭ ...ᏚᏂᎩᏍᏗ ᎾᎥ *bus* ᏃᏭ ᏦᎩᎷᏨ ᏦᎦᏣᏅ Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᏒᎾᎴ ᎨᎲ ᏓᏳᏬᏂᏒ Weaver ᎯᏯᏅᏓᏗ ᎤᏬᏂᏎ ᏬᎩᏯᏅᎲ, “Jim Proctor, Julio Pritchett, Walter Mink, Charlie Shell, come to the office,” ᎠᏗᎲ ᏙᏳ, ᏬᎩᏴᎲ “ᏕᏣᏕᎶᏆᎡᏍ ᏒᎯ?” ᎣᎪᎮᎸ ᏃᏭ ᎣᎦᏓᎵᏍᎪᏁ “ᎥᎥ ᏙᎦᏕᎶᏆᎡᏒ” ...”ᏝᏕ’Ᏺ ᎨᎢ ᎠᏭᏃ ᎠᏓᎨ.Ꮧ ᏫᏣᎦ,ᏛᏅᎢ ᎠᎹᏱ ᏫᏥᎷᎨ” ᏬᎩᎷᏨ ᎢᎬᏂᏭ ᎨᏒ ᏂᏓᏳᏍᏓᏅᎯᏓ “ᎥᎾ Ꮣ--ᎥᎾ ᏓᏥ,ᎩᎸ Ꭺ.ᎩᏭ ᎡᎵᏍᏗ ᏂᏣᏓᏅᏛᏅ,” ᎣᎪᎮᎸ
segments.transliteration: ayahena saquu yuwagada sgisquu tsinogadvnele nadv *hooky* tsinogadvnele na tsuweyv vnadv saquu tsinusdv itlugv amaya gadu vna tsogile nowu ...dunigisdi nav *bus* nowu tsogilutsv tsogatsanv na’e svnale gehv dayuwonisv Weaver hiyanvdadi uwonise wogiyanvhv, “Jim Proctor, Julio Pritchett, Walter Mink, Charlie Shell, come to the office,” adihv doyu, wogiyvhv “detsadeloquaes svhi?” ogohelv nowu ogadalisgone “vv dogadeloquaesv” ...”tlade’yo gei awuno adage.di witsaga,dvnvi amayi witsiluge” wogilutsv igvniwu gesv nidayusdanvhida “vna da--vna datsi,gilv go.giwu elisdi nitsadanvdvnv,” ogohelv
segments.translation: We did that, too, one time—we played hooky. Do you remember there was a creek running close by, and a tree with a hook on it and we would sit there all day, until it was time to leave. Then we’d go back to school to get on the bus. The next morning Weaver, you remember him, spoke and called our names—“Jim Proctor, Julio Pritchett, Walter Mink, Charlie Shell, come to the office,” he said. We went in, “Did you all go to school yesterday?” he asked. We lied, “Yeah, we went to school.” “No you didn’t. Look out the window, we could see where you all were at the water.” We looked, and you could see right where we were. “You all looked like a bunch of crows sitting on that tree,” he said.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ’Ꭷ ᏙᎲ? ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ *cameras*-Ꭲ ᏚᏂᎭ, ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ ᏙᎲ? Ꮭ ᎮᎾ--Ꮭ ᎮᎾ Ꮿ-- Ꮭ ᎮᎾ ᏯᎾᏗᏍᎦᏢᎦᏃ ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ ᏧᎾᏕᎶᏆᏍᏗ ᏗᏕᎶᏆ ᏳᏰᎸ...ᎠᏯ ᎮᎾ--ᎠᏯ ᎮᎾ ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ ᏗᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎸ ᏚᎶᏒ *y’know eighteen* ᏯᏩᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ *sixty—sixty four* ᎤᏕᏘᏴᏌᏗᏒ Greenleaf ᏓᎩᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎴ *75 cents/hr* ᎣᏦᏢᏍᎬ *$6.75 a day* ᎣᏍᏓᏅ ᏦᎩᏰᎸᏒ ᏍᏊ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ *gas*Ꮕ ᏔᎵᏍᎪᎯ ᎢᏯᏓᏅᏖᏗᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ *gallon* ᎾᎯᏳ *eighteen cents* ᎴᏱᎩ *fifty cents* ᏱᏣᏝ ᎪᎯᏗ ᏯᏟᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎬ)
segments.transliteration: asenv’ka dohv? gohi tsigi *cameras*-i duniha, gohi tsigi dohv? tla hena--tla hena ya-- tla hena yanadisgatlvgano gohi tsigi tsunadeloquasdi dideloqua yuyelv...aya hena--aya hena doyu hena digilvwisdanelv dulosv *y’know eighteen* yawadetiyvda tsigehv *sixty—sixty four* udetiyvsadisv Greenleaf dagilvwisdanele *75 cents/hr* otsotlvsgv *$6.75 a day* osdanv tsogiyelvsv squu nahiyu tsigehv *gas*nv talisgohi iyadanvtediwu tsigehv *gallon* nahiyu *eighteen cents* leyigi *fifty cents* yitsatla gohidi yatlida tsigehv (uyetsisgv)
segments.translation: But really, nowadays, they have cameras. You can’t hide now at school. If you’re trying to go to school… But me, I was a worker. Since I was 18 years old. ’64 I worked at Greenleaf and was making seventy-five cents an hour. Six dollars seventy-five a day. But we thought we were doing good. Gas was twenty cents a gallon then, or eighteen cents. If you had fifty cents, you could run around.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about you? Where did you go to school?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Bell.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Bell. Is that where you grew up, too?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ...’Ꮧ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᎢᏅ ᎨᎲ Salem-Ꭲ ᏝᎨ? ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᎢᎾ ᎨᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ...
segments.transliteration: vv...’di yawanata inv gehv Salem-i tlage? yawanata ina gehv tsigehv...
segments.translation: Mm-hmm. I don’t know where it is. It might be at Salem.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ...ᎤᎪᏛ ᎨᎵ ᏙᏳ ᎠᏯ Salem-Ꭲ ᏗᏢ ᏏᎾ Bell-Ꭲ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ...ugodv geli doyu aya Salem-i ditlv sina Bell-i gehv
segments.translation: It’s more in Salem than Bell, I think. There’s a church there but we go to Chuculate Church.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: It was my home—our home.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: It’s more in Salem than Bell, I think. There’s a church there but we go to Chuculate Church.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏅᏱ ᎣᏓᎸ ᏥᎦᏁᎳᏃ ᎤᏴᎸᏂᏍ ᎦᏙ ᎤᏍᏓᏂᏙᎴ ᏕᏍᏛᏩᏛ.Ꭾ?
segments.transliteration: nvyi odalv tsiganelano uyvlvnis gado usdanidole desdvwadv.he?
segments.translation: He lived in Rocky Mountain; you lived in Bell. How did y'all meet?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yeah, probably at Stilwell. We were in Stilwell.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s where you saw her?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Boy, “ᏍᎩᏛ ᏫᏓᏥᏯᏅᎯ,” ᏤᎵᏎᏍ? ... ‘Ꮩ Ꭲ--‘Ꮩ--ᎥᎾ ᏥᏥᏁᎸ ᏅᏲᏓᎸ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎬᏯᏛᏁᏗ ᎨᏒ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎢᏣᏛᏁᎮ ᏕᏣᏛ.ᏏᏗᏒ?
segments.transliteration: Boy, “sgidv widatsiyanvhi,” tselises? ... ‘do i--‘do--vna tsitsinelv nvyodalv ‘do usdi gvyadvnedi gesv ‘do usdi itsadvnehe detsadv.sidisv?
segments.translation: You thought, “That’s who I’m going to marry.” Where you lived, at Rocky Mountain, what did you all do when you were growing up?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: You mean, when we were kids?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎢᎾᎨᏛ ᎣᏤᎲ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᏳᎩᏨᏅ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏬᏥᎶᏍᎬ ᏃᏊᎴᏅ Wauhillau ᏥᎩ ᏣᎾᏔᏍ ᎥᎾ ᎨᎰ Wauhillau?
segments.transliteration: inagedv otsehv nigohilv yugitsvnv inage wotsilosgv noquulenv Wauhillau tsigi tsanatas vna geho Wauhillau?
segments.translation: We were in the woods all the time. In the mornings, we would go to the woods. And also Wauhilia, do you know where that is?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎾ’Ᏼ ᏙᎦᏘᏁᎨᏒ ᎣᎩᏥ ᎾᏅ Paul Cooksey ᎤᏥ ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᏣᎥ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏒᎾᎴ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ Ꮔ-ᏄᎧᎸᏨᎾᏃ ᎠᎹᏱ ᏬᏥᎶᏍᎬ ᎾᏅ ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᎥᎾ ᎠᏁᎯ ᏙᎦᎵᎪᏒ ᎨᎲ *noodles*Ꮫ ᎾᏅᏁᎲ Ꮎ ᏚᏍᏓᎦᎸ...ᏚᏍᏓᎦᎸ ᏍᎩ ᎠᏯ ᏝᏙᏲ--Ꮭ ᏙᏳ ᏯᏩᏚᎵᎮ ᎠᏯ ᏍᎩ ᏯᏩᏛᏁᏗ uh...ᎾᏛ Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏰᎵᎮ ᏌᏊ ᎠᏧᏣ Ketcher ᏧᏙᎢᏓ Ed Ketcher ᏏᎮᎾ ᎥᎾ ᏗᏁᎯ Ꭺ.Ꭿ ᏥᎩ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏝᏃ ᏙᏣᏓᏩᏛ.ᎯᏙᎰ ... Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ Ꮽ--ᏭᎵ,--ᏭᎵ,ᏍᏆᏛᏛᎮ ᎾᎮᎾ Paul Cooksey Ꮎ Roy Cooksey ᎨᎲ ᏝᏃ ᏯᏁᎯ ᎡᏧᎳ ... ᎡᏧᎳ ᏙᎦᎵᎪᎵᏙᎴ
segments.transliteration: vna’yv dogatinegesv ogitsi nanv Paul Cooksey utsi nigada otsav eladi svnale yinuli,stanv nu-nukalvtsvnano amayi wotsilosgv nanv anitsutsa vna anehi dogaligosv gehv *noodles*dv nanvnehv na dusdagalv...dusdagalv sgi aya tladoyo--tla doyu yawadulihe aya sgi yawadvnedi uh...nadv tla osda yelihe saquu atsutsa Ketcher tsudoida Ed Ketcher sihena vna dinehi go.hi tsigi aseno tlano dotsadawadv.hidoho ... tla yawanata wu--wuli,--wuli,squadvdvhe nahena Paul Cooksey na Roy Cooksey gehv tlano yanehi etsula ... etsula dogaligolidole
segments.translation: Wauhilia that’s where they took us. Our mom and Paul Cooksey’s mom, we were all walking. When morning came, before the sun had come up, we would walk across the water. The boys that were with us, from there, they were noodling snakes from the holes on the bank. But I wasn’t about to do that. One boy, named Ketcher, he didn’t really care, Ed Ketcher. They still live over there, but we don’t visit each other anymore. It ended. And Paul Cooksey and Roy Cooksey, they are both gone now. We ran around with both of them.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How about you? Growing up in Bell…

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What did you all do?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᎤᏠᏱᏭ ᏌᎷᏱᏭ ᏙᏣᏁᎶᏂᏙᎸ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏦᏥᏲᏟ... “Ꮭ ᎰᏩ ᎫᏍᏗ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎲ...ᎬᎩᏃᎮᏗ
segments.transliteration: utloyiwu saluyiwu dotsanelonidolv nigada tsotsiyotli... “tla howa gusdi yawanata,” tsiyohehv...gvginohedi
segments.translation: Just the same. All of us children just played around in the woods all day. “I don’t know anything I could tell,” I tell him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏍᎾᎭ? Ꭺ.Ꭿ ᏥᎩ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏧᎾᏁᎵ;ᏙᏗ ᏧᏂᎭ, ᎮᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏱᎩᎾᎡ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: ayasnaha? go.hi tsigi diniyotli tsunaneli;dodi tsuniha, hesdi sgiyusdi yiginae dohv?
segments.translation: Today all the toys the kids have to play with, we didn’t have all that stuff, when we were little.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: Huh uh. segments.translation: We didn’t have television. We didn’t even have electric. Not until about ’71 we moved by Levi Johnson. That’s when we got electric and plumbing. The water came in through a pump in the kitchen to wash dishes. But that’s all they had back then, we had to use an outhouse. I don’t know if I’m the only one that grew up that poor.

segments.translation: Was it a little better?

ᎤᏃᎯᎸᏍᏔᏅ ᎣᏥᎨ.ᎲᏒᏛ ᎩᏟ ᎤᏔᎾ ᎤᎾᏝᎥ Ꭴ’Ꮯ ᎢᎦᏘ ᎾᎥ ᎣᎦᏓᎸ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏓᎨ.ᎯᏐ ‘Ꮲ ᏳᎩ.ᎸᏅ ᏍᎩᏛ ᏭᎩ.Ꮅ;ᏛᏃᎰ...ᏭᎩ.Ꮅ,ᏔᏅ ᏅᏱᏛ ᏙᏣᏬᏂᎰ ‘ᏢᏴ ᏧᏙᏒ Ꮎ ᏚᏯᏪᏦᏅ Ꮎ ᎤᎫᎫ ᏍᎩᏭᏛ ᏃᎦᏛᎿᏕᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎣᎩᏰᎸᏒ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ

segments.translation: They were living better. Because there was water inside the house. But they used firewood. I think just about everybody used firewood. We were cutting wood, my nephew and I. And we were selling them for heating, four dollars for half a rick. But five dollars a rick to cook with. We felt good about it, back then. There was nothing else to do. I mentioned I was working at Greenleaf. They gave us Piecework… May Sanders, Melvin Campbell—we were setting the flower pots. And the more rows we finished we got a one-hundred and twenty [dollar] check. We really felt good about it, back then. It was really good getting paid like that. But today, it’s not as good. You can’t buy anything with just that much money. We were in a bad spot because we couldn’t afford college. That’s what is lacking. These young kids need to go to college, they are using too many drugs nowadays. If they go to college—I’m not saying it will stop—but they could get something from it. There are a lot of things nowadays. But as we were growing up… The children are not doing exercise today. They are just watching their phones. They are sitting like this [indicates] they probably don’t even know we came to visit or not. Cause they are just watching the phone. I’m not saying I’m different because sometimes I watch my phone too. I mean, when it’s something important, but not just to play with it. Back then, we always found something to do. There was an owl that flew by, we chased it and my neighbor had a big dog. That’s the one that chased the owl, and when it landed on a tree the dog would tree it and we would throw rocks at it. One day, it fell from the tree when it got wore out, that owl. That’s all we had to do, but we were having fun.

segments.translation: Yeah, they were everywhere. It was really interesting when I was growing up. If a deer walked by in the yard it was really interesting to see a deer. But nowadays there are so many around.

segments.translation: Uh uh, there weren’t that many. I don’t know what happened, why there are so many now. Sometimes where I live there are about four standing around in the yard, eating. All I can do is look at them today. So I just go back to sleep. They come early in the morning about two o’clock.

segments.text: ᏙᏣᏛ.ᏓᏍᏙᏅᎮᎡ ᏦᎩᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏙᎩᎸᏂᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꭺ.Ꭿ ᏥᎩ “ᎮᏍᏗ! *Be still. Be quiet.*” ᏍᎩᏭ ᎢᎦ ᏱᎾᏂᏪ ᏃᏭᏅ ᏧᎾᏔᎾ ᎨᏍᏗ...ᎨᏍᏗ ᏯᏂᏅᏍᏓᏕᏃ ᎰᏩ ᎠᏯ ᎮᎾ ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ ᏲᎩᏑᎵᎪᏣ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ᎾᏛ ᏱᏬᎩᎪᎥ Ꮎ ᏆᎾ--ᏆᎾ ᎤᏱᏢᏅ ᏱᏭ--ᏱᏫᏄᏮᏂᏕᏌ ᎾᏛ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ᏲᏦᎯᏳᎲᎨ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎠᏎᏅᎧ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᎬᏅ ᏙᎲ “ᎦᏥᏅᏁᎮᏍᏗ” ᎠᏗᎲ ᎪᏪᎵ ᎤᎭᎨᏙ ᏯᎦᏎᏍᏔᎾ
segments.transliteration: dotsadv.dasdonvhee tsogigayvlige dogilvnidi gehv go.hi tsigi “hesdi! *Be still. Be quiet.*” sgiwu iga yinaniwe nowunv tsunatana gesdi...gesdi yaninvsdadeno howa aya hena doyu hena yogisuligotsa gi.la nadv yiwogigov na quana--quana uyitlvnv yiwu--yiwinuwvnidesa nadv gi.la yotsohiyuhvge nahiyu asenvka sgina nigvnv dohv “gatsinvnehesdi” adihv goweli uhagedo yagasestana
segments.translation: We always listened to our parents. We used to get whippings but today all they say is, “Hesdi! Be still! Be quiet!” They’re not making them mind. We listened to our parents, and when we see him take off that peach switch—that’s when we really minded him. But that’s what it says, the Bible: be whipping the kids.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎾᏕ ᎡᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏂᎪᎯ--ᎤᎸᏉᏛ’Ꮥ ᏱᎦᏓ ᎮᎾ ᎤᏓᎸᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ “ᏫᏱ, ᎦᏂᏍᏘ!” ᏯᏓᏙᏌ ᎣᏩᏌ ᎠᏩ-Ꮹ-ᏩᏛ.Ꮧ ᎡᏣᎸᏂᏍᏙᏗ ᏝᏍᏊ ᎬᏳᏩᎨ.Ꮹ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏂᎳᏫᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᏲᏤᏙ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᏫᏂᎷᏨ ᏓᎬᎸᏂᎵ,” ᏯᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏭ ᏔᎵ ᎢᎦ ᎤᎶᏒ ᏱᏩᏅᏓᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ “Ꭷ ᎦᎾᎦᏍᏘ ᏫᏱ,” ᏯᏬᏌ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv nade etsi tsigehv nigohi--ulvquodv’de yigada hena udalvsdi gehv “wiyi, ganisti!” yadadosa owasa awa-wa-wadv.di etsalvnisdodi tlasquu gvyuwage.wa tsigehv tsunilawisdi’e yotsedo tsigehv “winilutsv dagvlvnili,” yada tsigehv eliwu tali iga ulosv yiwanvdada tsigehv “ka ganagasti wiyi,” yawosa tsigehv
segments.translation: Yeah. That’s what the Bible says. But my mom, I think she just really liked to whip us. [laughs] She’d say, “Go get the stick,” you had to go get it yourself for her to use to whip you. She would not forget it either. We would be at church and she would say, “I’m gonna whip you when we get home.” Even about two days later she would remember and she’d tell me, “Go get the stick!”

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᎢᏡᎬ ᏲᏥᎩ.Ꮈ ᎨᎲ “ᏕᏥᏲᏏᏐᏅᏛ ᏕᏣᏠᏒ,” ᏣᏗᏪ ᏤᎲ ᏫᎦᎶᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏱᏪᎾ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ ᏗᏢ Ꮎ ᎣᎩᏥ ᏙᏳ,ᏅᏍᏊ Ꮭ ᏳᏮᎨᏩᏍᎨ ᏙᏳ, ᎮᎾ Ꮟ ᏙᎩᎸᏂᎮ
segments.transliteration: ayadv itlugv yotsigi.lv gehv “detsiyosisonvdv detsatlosv,” tsadiwe tsehv wigalohi tsigehv yiwena didanelv ditlv na ogitsi doyu,nvsquu tla yuwvgewasge doyu, hena si dogilvnihe
segments.translation: Us, we would climb a tree and she would say, “When y’all get hungry, you all will come down.” She would walk off back toward the house, but sure enough she didn’t forget, she did whip us.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They didn’t whip us easy either, they really whipped us good.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Very.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is that what you went through, too?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Huh?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is that what you went through, too?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: Huh uh. ᎮᏍᏗ ᎰᏩ ᏦᎩᎸᎮ ᏱᎨᎮ
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. hesdi howa tsogilvhe yigehe
segments.translation: Uh uh. We didn’t hardly get any whippings.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh! You were all good kids.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: [Laughing] No!

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Jerry, ᎥᎾᏭᏍ ᎢᎦ ᏅᏲᏓᎸ ᎮᎾ ᏗᏣᏓᏅᏎ ᎭᏢᏃ ᎯᏁᎳ ᏃᏊ ᎨᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Jerry, vnawus iga nvyodalv hena ditsadanvse hatlvno hinela noquu gehv?
segments.translation: Jerry, did you just move from Nvyodalv?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: I live close by Salem now.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Salem.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: Ꮎ ᎤᏙᏓ ᏧᏁᎳᏛ ᎾᎥ ᎾᏛ ᎠᎦᏴᎵᎨ ᏤᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᎵᏏ...ᎤᎵᏏᏛ Ꮟ ᏴᏓ ᎠᏎ ᏌᎵ ᏝᎨ.?
segments.transliteration: na udoda tsuneladv nav nadv agayvlige tsehv na ulisi...ulisidv si yvda ase sali tlage.?
segments.translation: By where her dad used to live. When the old lady was alive, her grandma, is she still alive? Sali, right?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ ᏥᏩᏂᏁᎳᏛ ᎦᏙᎯ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏦᎦᎾᏁᏍᎨᎲ ’73 ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏕᏘᏴᏌᏗᏒ ᎣᎩᏂᏴᏢ Ꮎ Ꮟ ᎥᎾᏭ Ꮟ ᎣᏍᏕᎰ
segments.transliteration: sgi hena tsiwanineladv gadohi nahiyu tsogananesgehv ’73 tsigehv udetiyvsadisv oginiyvtlv na si vnawu si osdeho
segments.translation: She gave us some land. That’s when we built our house. It was in the year ’73. And we’ve lived there ever since.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And it’s almost 50 years?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏍᎩᎢᏴ ᎥᎥ ᎪᎯᏗᏛ...ᎪᎯ ᏥᎩ ᎤᎯᏐᏙ ᏂᏗᎦᎵᏍᏙᏗᏅ ᏣᎾᏔᏍ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ Ꮭ ᏯᏂ---ᎠᏂᏓᏩᏛ.ᎯᏙᎯ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏯᏂᎷᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꭺ.Ꭿ ᏥᎩ “ᏃᏭᏛ ᎣᎬᏌ ᏙᎦᏓᏘᎾᎥ,” ᏯᎾᏓᏛ ᏃᏭ
segments.transliteration: sgiiyv vv gohididv...gohi tsigi uhisodo nidigalisdodinv tsanatas diniyotli tla yani---anidawadv.hidohi tsigehv agvyi yaniluga tsigehv go.hi tsigi “nowudv ogvsa dogadatinav,” yanadadv nowu
segments.translation: That’s it. Long time. But today, it is lonesome there. The kids used to visit us but today they say “We have our own kids.”

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They hardly come visit anymore.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: But they did come last Saturday. They brought us some chicken to eat.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: So you didn’t have to cook?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Uh huh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You liked auctions, don’t you, Jerry?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏗ ᎠᏪᏓᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᏃ ᎨᏍᏗ ᏙᏳ ᎤᏟ ᎢᎦ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ ᏱᎩ.ᏩᏍᎪ ᏣᎾᏔ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎨᎵ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ᏯᎩ.ᏩᎯ, ...ᏳᏓᎭ ᏍᏊ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏄᏰᎵ,ᏛᎾ ᏯᎩ.ᏩᎯ, ᎣᏍᏓ
segments.transliteration: agilvquodi awedasdi aseno gesdi doyu utli iga nigalisdihv yigi.wasgo tsanata gi.lo osda yigeli gi.la yagi.wahi, ...yudaha squu osda nuyeli,dvna yagi.wahi, osda
segments.translation: Yeah, but I hardly ever go now. And I don’t really buy anything unless I think it’s something worth buying. Sometimes I feel like I buy something for nothing.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s what happens to me too.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: It just sits at the house.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: This Saturday, they’re having an auction at Muskogee.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I was thinking about going.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: That is kind of a long ways.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I even go further sometimes, all the way to Inola.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: So you hang around that far?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎥᎾᏛ’Ᏺ ᎤᏔᎾ ᏧᎾ,ᏅᏃ ᎨᎲ ‘ᏙᏓᏆᏓ ᎯᏍᎩ, ᏅᎩᏅ ᏚᎾᏂᎩᏍᏗᏓ ᎠᏂᏁᎨ ᎥᎾ ᎣᏍᏕᏙ ᏳᏓᎭ
segments.transliteration: vnadv’yo utana tsuna,nvno gehv ‘dodaquada hisgi, nvginv dunanigisdida aninege vna osdedo yudaha
segments.translation: That’s where they have a big [auction] all day long. They have about four or five stands for auctions. We go there sometimes.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: CharlieᎾ ᏂᎯᎧ--ᏂᎯᎧ ᏂᎯᏛ *brother and sister* ᎤᎪᏓ ᏂᏣᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: Charliena nihika--nihika nihidv *brother and sister* ugoda nitsali,stanv dohv?
segments.translation: Charlie, there were a lot of you all, in your family—brother and sister?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ ᎾᎢᏅ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ ᏄᏍᏛ ᏙᎲ? ᎨᏍᏗ--ᎨᏍᏗ--ᎨᏍᏗ ᏔᎵᏭ ᏦᎢᏭ ᎴᏱᎦ Ꮩ-ᎠᏂ-ᏙᏳ, ᏯᏂᏍᏆᏗ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ayasquu utloyi nainv squu utloyi sgi hena nusdv dohv? gesdi--gesdi--gesdi taliwu tsoiwu leyiga do-ani-doyu, yanisquadi nahiyu tsigehv
segments.translation: We were the same, there was a lot of us. Her family was the same too. That’s how it was. They didn’t have just two or three, they didn’t quit there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many are there of you all? Or how many were there?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏃᎩᎥᏛ--ᏃᏥᎥᏛ Ꮳ.ᏁᎳᏛᏢ ᎣᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏂᎦᏓᏭ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏌᏭ--...ᏔᎵ...ᏔᎵ Ꮭ ᏯᏁᎯ ᏌᏭ ᎣᎩᏙ Ꮭ ᏰᎯ ᏧᏔᏂᏓ ᏌᏭ’Ᏺ ᎣᏥᏍᏗᎬ’Ᏺ ᎣᏂ ᎡᎯ ᏧᏲᎱᏒ ᎯᎳᏴ’Ꮥ ᏧᏍᏆᏛ ᏧᏕᏘᏴᏌᏗᎲ ᎡᎵᏭᏛ *4 years*Ꮲ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: nogivdv--notsivdv tsa.neladvtlv ogali,stanv nigadawu gehv aseno sawu--...tali...tali tla yanehi sawu ogido tla yehi tsutanida sawu’yo otsisdigv’yo oni ehi tsuyohusv hilayv’de tsusquadv tsudetiyvsadihv eliwudv *4 years*tlv tsigehv
segments.translation: There were eight of us. But today two are gone. Our older sister is gone. There’s one younger sister that’s gone too. I don’t remember when it was, about four years I think, is when she died.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did they all speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: All of them?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: Ꮎ’Ꭱ Ᏺ’ Ꮭ...ᏌᏭ’Ᏺ ᏱᎦᏬᏂᎯ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏍᏗᎧᏂ ᎠᏰᏟᏴ ᏦᏍᏓ--ᎣᏍᏓᏝᏅᏢ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ ᎨᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᎢᎦ ᎦᏬᏂᎯ ᏱᎨᎮ ᏳᏰᏍᏓᎭ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ᏣᎾᏔᏍ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎤᏬᏂ--ᏯᎴᎾ ᎦᏬᏂᎯ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎦ)
segments.transliteration: na’e yo’ tla...sawu’yo yigawonihi gehv na usdikani ayetliyv tsosda--osdatlanvtlv asesgini gesdi’e iga gawonihi yigehe yuyesdaha gi.la tsanatas tsalagi uwoni--yalena gawonihi (uyetsisga)
segments.translation: Uh huh. There was one, the younger half-brother, did not talk unless he was drunk, then he would start talking. [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And you, how many were you all?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Eleven.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Eleven.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did they speak Cherokee?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: All of them?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s all you spoke to each other in your house?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Who were your parents, Jerry?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏦᎩᎦᏴᎵᎨᏛ ᎠᏂ-Adair Ꮎ ᎣᎩᏥᏏ ᏗᏢ ᎾᎿᎾ ... ᎣᎩᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎨᏍᏗ’Ꭱ Ᏺ’ ᏯᏆᎾᏔ ᎠᏯ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎤᏙᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎢᎦ ᎮᎾ ... ‘ᎨᏴ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ ᎾᎥ--ᎾᎥ Ꮩ’ ᏄᎾᏓᎸ ᎨᏒ ᎠᏂ-Liver’s ᎣᎩᏠᏱᏅ ᏍᏊ ... Ꮎ ᎦᏙ.Ꭶ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ Ᏹ.ᏯᏅᏓᏗ...
segments.transliteration: tsogigayvligedv ani-Adair na ogitsisi ditlv nahnana ... ogidoda tsigehv gesdi’e yo’ yaquanata aya sginana udoda gehv iga hena ... ‘geyv asesgini nav--nav do’ nunadalv gesv ani-Liver’s ogitloyinv squu ... na gado.ga tsigehv tla yawanata yi.yanvdadi...
segments.translation: On our mom’s side, they were Adair’s. And my dad, I don’t know who his family was, cause they were too far down the line. But the nearest kin were the Livers. So we’re kin to them too. That Gatoga, that was, I don’t know if you remember him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah... Yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ...ᏍᎩᎾ ᎢᎦ ᎾᎥ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏛᏂ,Ꮧ ᎤᏂᏰᎸ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎣᎩᏙᏓ...ᏥᏈᏍᏙᏒ ᏓᏁᎯ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎣᎦᏓᏛᏂ,Ꮧ ᎠᏂ-Adair, Ketcher’s, ᎾᎿ Fourkiller’s ᏂᎦᏓ ᏥᏈᏍᏙᏒ ᎠᏁᎯ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎣᏣᏓᏛᏂ,Ꮧ
segments.transliteration: ...sgina iga nav tsuna,dadvni,di uniyelv gehv aya ogidoda...tsiquisdosv danehi osda ogadadvni,di ani-Adair, Ketcher’s, nahna Fourkiller’s nigada tsiquisdosv anehi osda otsadadvni,di
segments.translation: They say he was real close to my dad, we have a lot of kinfolk. There’s Adairs, Ketchers, and Fourkillers. There’s just a bunch of us.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That one you called Gatoga, they say he was a Liver?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yeah. Liver… Uwelv.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏚᏳᎪᏛ ᏱᎩᏂ...ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᏛᏂ,Ꮧ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎩ ᎠᏯ ᎮᎾ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ ᏗᏮᏂ,Ꮧ ᏍᎩᎾ Liver’s...ᎩᎾᏕᏞᏍᏗ Ᏺ’ ᎠᏯ
segments.transliteration: duyugodv yigini...gohusdi dina,dadvni,di sgi tsigi aya hena gohusdi hena diwvni,di sgina Liver’s...ginadetlesdi yo’ aya
segments.translation: To be honest, we must be kin. Because we are kin to the Liver’s. But don’t be telling people.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: So you don’t want people to know we’re kin? [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯ ᎮᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ...ᏂᎦᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏰᏟ ᎣᏍᏓᏝᏅᏟ ᏔᎵ ᏗᎬᎩᏙ ᎠᏰᏟ ᎠᏁᎯ Ꮶ’ᎠᏚ ᎮᎾ ᏍᎩ ᏃᏥ’Ꭱ Ᏺ’
segments.transliteration: aya hena nigada...nigada gehv ayetli osdatlanvtli tali digvgido ayetli anehi tso’adu hena sgi notsi’e yo’
segments.translation: Me, all of us counting half-siblings, there are thirteen of us.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Is that right?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎯᎢ’Ᏺ ᏌᏊᏅ ᏒᎯᏭ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏌᏊ ᎠᏩᏓᏚᏥᏴ ᏁᎲᎾ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏓ
segments.transliteration: hii’yo saquunv svhiwu tsigehv saquu awadadutsiyv nehvna nigalisda
segments.translation: Yesterday, one of my nephews passed away.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah…

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏍ ᏳᏍᏗ Ꮎ Sam ᏁᏙᎲᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ?
segments.transliteration: sgis yusdi na Sam nedohvna tsigehv?
segments.translation: Really? Is that why Sam wasn’t here?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah. We went over there.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: What was wrong with him? Was he sick?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Cancer.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ... Ꮎ ᎤᏲᏎᎴ *chemo* ᏣᏃᎮᎲ ᎾᏅ ᏐᎢ ᎤᏲᏎᎴ Ꮭ ᏳᏚᎸᎮ ... ᎠᏥᏰᏝᎴ ᎮᎾ’Ᏺ ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ...ᎠᏎᏃ Ꮭ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏳᏂᏂᎩᏐᏅ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏲᏎᎸ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᎲ ... ᎾᏛ ᎪᎯᏓ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏥᏄᎵᏍᏓᏁᎵᏓ ... ᎥᎾᏭᏍ ᏅᏲᏓᎸ ᏓᏳᎾᏓᎴᏅ ᏗᎨᏣᎦᏴᎵᎨ?
segments.transliteration: vv ... na uyosele *chemo* tsanohehv nanv soi uyosele tla yudulvhe ... atsiyetlale hena’yo aseno tla...aseno tla nigada yuninigisonv sgina uyoselv sgina gehv ... nadv gohida sgina tsinulisdanelida ... vnawus nvyodalv dayunadalenv digetsagayvlige?
segments.translation: He didn’t want to do chemo. He didn’t want to do the ‘other’ one. He didn’t want it. He had surgery, but they didn’t get all of it. He was sick for a long time. Nvyodalv, is that where your parents came from?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: *Well*...Ꮭ ᏱᎨᎵ ... ᏍᏗᎵᏪᎵᏛ ‘Ꮲ Ꮎ *Adair County Park* ᏥᏄᏍᏗ ... ᎥᎾ ᎮᎾ ᎣᎩᏚᏓ ᎤᏤᎵ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎦᏙᎯ ᎠᏂᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᎨᎲ *spring*Ꮽ ᎢᎦ ᏄᏍᏕ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎾᎥ ᏄᎾᏓᎸ ᎠᏂᎫ.ᎩᏎᎲ ᏣᏗᎲ ᏃᏊ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᎤᏂᏩᎭ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎤᏂᏩᎭ ᏍᎩᎾᎾᏃ ᏍᏘᎩᏓ *pond*ᏳᏍᏗ ᏄᏅᏁᎸ Ꮎ ᎠᎹ ᏥᎦᏁᎠ Ꮎ *Adair County Park* ... Ꮩ’ ᎮᎾ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ ᎦᏙᎯ ᎤᎲ ᎣᎩᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏎᏍᎩᏂ “you’re gonna have to sell one of them ᎨᎩ--ᎡᏣᏍᏕᎵᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏱᎬᏣᏍᏕᎳ Ꭹ.Ꮃ 40 acres ᏱᏣᏂ,ᏗᎾ, this one, Rocky Mt., or ᎥᎾ,” ᎠᎪᏎᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ Ꮎ *Adair Country Park* ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎤᎬᏫᏳᏒ ᏭᏂᏂ,ᏗᏅᏒ ᏗᎦᏚᎲ ᎾᎥ ... ᎥᎾ ᏕᎦᏂᏏᏅ ᏭᎵ,ᏍᏛ ᏗᏢ Ꮟ ᎣᎩᏚᏓ ᎠᎾᏝᏅᏝ Ꮟ ᎥᎾᎾ
segments.transliteration: *Well*...tla yigeli ... sdiliwelidv ‘tlv na *Adair County Park* tsinusdi ... vna hena ogiduda utseli gehv sgina gadohi aninohesgv gehv *spring*wu iga nusde tsiquisdi nav nunadalv anigu.gisehv tsadihv noquu gi.lo uniwaha sginana uniwaha sginanano stigida *pond*yusdi nunvnelv na ama tsiganea na *Adair County Park* ... do’ hena gohiga tsigehv tsiquisdi hena gadohi uhv ogidoda tsigehv asesgini “you’re gonna have to sell one of them gegi--etsasdelidi gehv tla yigvtsasdela gi.la 40 acres yitsani,dina, this one, Rocky Mt., or vna,” agoselv tsadihv na *Adair Country Park* sginana ugvwiyusv wunini,dinvsv digaduhv nav ... vna deganisinv wuli,sdv ditlv si ogiduda anatlanvtla si vnana
segments.translation: Well... I don’t think so. Our grandpa owned land in Stilwell, by Adair County Park. They say there was a spring there and all the neighbors came to get water there. But when people bought the land they made a pond. And that pond is still there by Adair County Park. A long time ago my dad had a lot of land but “You’re gonna have to sell one of them when you need help. We can’t help you unless you sell 40 acres of your land, this one or Rocky Mount.” They told him. So he sold the one at Adair County Park by the town. That’s where they’re buried, at the edge of the park, my grandpa and other kinfolk.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Park-T?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Ꮎ park ᎤᏩᏍᏓᏂᏢ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᏤᎵᏒ ᏱᎩ ᏧᎾ,ᏓᏂᏐᏗ ᎪᏢ
segments.transliteration: vv na park uwasdanitlv tla yawanata tselisv yigi tsuna,danisodi gotlv
segments.translation: Yeah. Park—where the fence is. I don’t know if you have noticed, there is a cemetery there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, right where they used to play ball?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yeah, straight from the ball park…

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎤᎾᏁᏦᏗ Ꭰ’Ꭿ ᏗᏢ ... Ꮭ’Ᏺ...Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᏯᏩᎾᏖ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ᎣᏂᏛ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ
segments.transliteration: vv unanetsodi a’hi ditlv ... tla’yo...tla’yo yawanate gi.la onidv awadelahosv sgi nusdidanv
segments.translation: This way is where the cemetery is. I didn’t know about this until not long ago.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: …That’s what I was think I remember.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Yeah, um...ᎠᏮᎨᏩᏍᎦ ᎦᏙ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎬᏯᏛ.Ꮧ ᎨᎲ um...ᏂᎯ ᎨᏒ Ꮎ ... Ꮸ-ᏨᏥᏍ ᎯᏕᎶᏆᎡᎴ ᏣᏓᏍᏓᏴᏗ? ᏗᎪᎦ--ᏨᏌᎨ?
segments.transliteration: Yeah, um...awvgewasga gado yusdi gvyadv.di gehv um...nihi gesv na ... tsv-tsvtsis hideloquaele tsadasdayvdi? digoga--tsvsage?
segments.translation: I’m forgetting what I was going to ask you. What about you? Did you learn to cook from your mom? Or on your own?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Probably my grandma. Mom wasn’t a cook.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You were just watching, or was she telling you how to do it?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: No. I was just watching. I was just helping around the kitchen, washing dishes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What did you like the best?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Dumplings.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎥᎥ. ᏝᏃ ᎤᏖᎸᎳᏗ ᏥᏓᏃ--ᏥᏓᏃᏢᏍᎦ ᏗᎦᎸᏅ Ꮭ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ Ᏹ.Ꭶ,ᏔᎭ,?
segments.transliteration: vv. tlano utelvladi tsidano--tsidanotlvsga digalvnv tla sgiyusdi yi.ga,taha,?
segments.translation: They were good. And what about the grapes they’re using to make dumplings? Do you know how to make those?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: No?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᎠᎩᎵᏏ ᏁᏙᎸ ᎤᏪᏥ ᎯᏲᎵᎦ Stanley
segments.transliteration: nadv agilisi nedolv uwetsi hiyoliga Stanley
segments.translation: My niece, Nedolv’s daughter, Stanley do you know him?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏙᏳ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏧᏬᏢᏗ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎤᏖᎸᎳᏗ ᏗᎦᎸᏅ
segments.transliteration: doyu osda tsuwotlvdi sgiyusdi utelvladi digalvnv
segments.translation: She can make grape dumplings real good.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎾᏛ Viola ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏕᎦᏃᎯᎲ ᏍᎩᎾᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᏅ ᏣᎾᏔᏍ Ꮎ *bottle*Ꮽ ᎠᏟᏍᏓ *grape* ᎤᏮ,ᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: nadv Viola squu utloyiiyusdi tsideganohihv sginayusdi asenv tsanatas na *bottle*wu atlisda *grape* uwv,tanv
segments.translation: Also, Viola, she used to make some and bring them. But she had just used grape juice. You know, from a bottle?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh huh, yeah, uh huh.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎨᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ--ᎨᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ ᏫᏓᏤᏢ ᎨᎦᏗ ᏣᎾᏔᏍ ᎢᎾᎨ ᏗᎦ--ᏗᎦᏕᏓ ᎤᏂᏖᎸᎳᏗ ᎢᏳᏟᏭᏛ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏍᏊᏅ--ᏍᏊᏅ *bottle*Ꮽ ᎪᏢᏔᏅ ᏱᎩ
segments.transliteration: gesdi hena--gesdi hena widatsetlv gegadi tsanatas inage diga--digadeda unitelvladi iyutliwudv gehv aya gehv osda squunv--squunv *bottle*wu gotlvtanv yigi
segments.translation: But me, even the grapes that’s been picked, or from the bottle, it’s still good to me.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏎᏅ ᏝᎮᎾ ᏍᏊ ᎰᏩ ᏯᏁᎯ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: asenv tlahena squu howa yanehi dohv?
segments.translation: But now, there’s not hardly any grapes anymore.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: No there’s not any.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: You can’t find them anywhere.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎾᏛᎾ ᎠᏯ ᏗᏩᏛ.Ꮢ ᎧᏅᏥ ᎮᎾ ᎠᏃᏢᏍᎬ ᏍᏘᎩᏓ Ꮎ ᎠᎩᏠᎩ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ Ꮎ Paul (Cooksey) ᎤᏂᏥ ᎦᎷᎪᏛ ᎨᎲ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ ᏐᎯ ᏗᏰᎮ ᎾᏅ ᎯᎢ ᏂᎦᏘ ᏥᎦᎧᎲ Ꮎ ᎤᏂᏍᏙ.ᏍᏛ *stump*ᏳᏍᏗ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ *log* ᏍᎩᎾ ᎣᏍᏓ--ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎬᏁᎴ ᎨᏒ ᎢᎦ ᏱᎬᏅᎯᏓ ᎠᏍᏙ.ᏅᏍᏙᏗ ᎠᏅᏗᎲ ᎨᎲ ᎩᎳ ᏱᎪᎯᏗ ᏅᎩᎭ ᏱᏓᏂᏝ ... ᏞᏍᏗᏅᏍᏊ ᏱᏓᏂᏂ,ᏕᎨ ...ᏆᎾ ᎮᎾ ᏥᎩ ᏓᏂᏂ,ᏕᎬᏭ ᎢᎦ ᎨᎰ ... ᏙᏣᏗᏔᏍᎬᏛ
segments.transliteration: nadvna aya diwadv.sv kanvtsi hena anotlvsgv stigida na agitlogi iyusdi gehv na Paul (Cooksey) unitsi galugodv gehv didanelv sohi diyehe nanv hii nigati tsigakahv na unisdo.sdv *stump*yusdi yuli,stanv *log* sgina osda--osda yigvnele gesv iga yigvnvhida asdo.nvsdodi anvdihv gehv gila yigohidi nvgiha yidanitla ... tlesdinvsquu yidanini,dege ...quana hena tsigi danini,degvwu iga geho ... dotsaditasgvdv
segments.translation: Where I grew up they made kanvtsi. Paul’s mother was just like a mother to me. She would come to the house carrying walnuts. There was a stump-looking–log where they had smashed the walnuts. It was a good thing to use to smash the walnuts, it didn’t take them long. They would have about four kanvtsi [balls of pounded-nut meat]. And they weren’t selling them, they sold peaches. We were drinking it [kanvtsi].

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎧᏃᎾᏛ ᎠᏃᎮᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᎩᎭ ᎮᎾ ᎥᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏂᎯ
segments.transliteration: kanonadv anoheho sgina agiha hena vsgiyusdi nihi
segments.translation: Kanona they call it. I’ve got one like that. [A wooden mortar]

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎾᏍ Ꮎ...ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏦᎩᎲ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏯ ᎯᎢ ᏱᎦᏘ
segments.transliteration: nas na...sgi hena yusdi tsogihv squu aya hii yigati
segments.translation: That one… We had one like that too. About this tall [indicates].

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah, mine’s about this tall [indicates].

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏃᏭᏅ *cup*Ꮽ ᎾᏕ ᎨᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ *refridgerator* ᏲᎩᎮ ᏃᏭᏅᎿ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏂᎬᏁᎲ ᎦᏚ ᎣᎩᏥ Ꮎ ᏲᎦᏚᎵᎮ ᎧᏅᏥ ᏍᎩᏭ ᎫᏢᏍᎨ ᏙᏥᏟᏗᎮ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: nowunv *cup*wu nade gesdi hena *refridgerator* yogihe nowunvhna gohusdi yusdi nigvnehv gadu ogitsi na yogadulihe kanvtsi sgiwu gutlvsge dotsitlidihe tsigehv
segments.translation: Just a cup… We didn’t have a refrigerator. My mom just put it in something and when we wanted it we just put it in cups.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏌᏊ ᏍᎪᎯ ᏚᏩᏍᎪ ᎠᎭᏂ ᏓᎵᏆ ᎡᎯ Ꮎ ᎠᏂᏣᎦᏓ ᏥᏓᏃᎮᎰ ᎥᎾ ᏓᏫᏗᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ’Ᏺ ᎠᏎ ᏓᏂᎿᏦᏍᏙᏍᎪ ᏓᏂᎿᏦᏍᏙᏍᎦ ᎠᏂᏔᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: saquu sgohi duwasgo ahani daliqua ehi na anitsagada tsidanoheho vna dawidiho sgina’yo ase danihnatsosdosgo danihnatsosdosga anitasgo
segments.translation: There’s one [person] that buys ten of them. And the ones they call Choctaws, that’s where they take them. But them, they make theirs sour. And that’s how they drink it. Real sour.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Some of them knows about this?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏥᎩ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏦᎢ ᎢᎦ ᏱᏣ;Ꮭ ᏙᎲ ‘Ꮲ ᏳᏲᏨ ... ᏍᎩ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏂᎩᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: tla yawanata aya gehv tla yigatsigi etsulaha tsoi iga yitsa;tla dohv ‘tlv yuyotsv ... sgi sgiyusdi anigisgo
segments.translation: Yeah, but I don’t know. I don’t think I would eat it like that. It’s just like it’s been sitting there about three days and got sour, that’s how they drank theirs.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ ᎡᎳᏗ ᏬᏣᎢᏒ--ᎣᏍᏓᎢᏒ’Ꮥ ᎠᏩᏓᏚᏥᏴ ᏗᏓᎾᏅ ᎣᎩᏁᏁᏗ *mile*Ꭲ’Ꮲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᏓᏁᎸ ᏙᎩᏂᏯᏅ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᎣᏍᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏦᎬᏂ,Ꮧ Ꮎ Ketcher ᏥᎦᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎨᎲ “ᏓᎦᏌᏂᏧ ᏱᏣᏚᎵ ᏱᏤᎾ ᏗᎾ,” ᎣᎩᏃᏎᎴ “ᎥᎥ. ᎥᎥ. ᏓᎦᏌᏂ Ꭿ’Ꭱ ᎪᎳ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎠᏎᏃ ᏬᎩᏂᎷᏨ ᎦᏙᎯ ᎤᏍᎪᏒ ᎤᏟᎢᎦ ᎤᏍᎪᎯᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎧᏁᏍᎦ ᎧᎵ ᏩᏐᎯᏢ ᎥᎾ ᏓᎦᏌᏂ ᎤᏠᏱᏭ’Ꮥ ᎢᏤ ᎡᎵᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᏓᎦᏌᏂ ᏛᏲᎩᏂᏁᎴ ᎠᏂᎦᏔᎾ’Ꭱ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏂᏍᏆᏂ,ᎪᏙᏗ ᎨᏍᏗ ᎮᎾ Ꮭ *freezer* ᏭᏂᎩᏍᏗ ᏱᎨᎮ *well, they couldn’t afford it* ᏝᎧ? ᎨᏍᏗᎧ?
segments.transliteration: saquu yuwaga,da eladi wotsaisv--osdaisv’de awadadutsiyv didananv oginenedi *mile*i’tlv tsigehv didanelv doginiyanv gi.lo osdinv squu tsogvni,di na Ketcher tsigadi sgina gehv “dagasanitsu yitsaduli yitsena dina,” oginosele “vv. vv. dagasani hi’e gola,” tsiyohelv aseno woginilutsv gadohi usgosv utliiga usgohida gehv kanesga kali wasohitlv vna dagasani utloyiwu’de itse elisdi gehv dagasani dvyogininele anigatana’e nahiyu tsigehv unisquani,gododi gesdi hena tla *freezer* wunigisdi yigehe *well, they couldn’t afford it* tlaka? gesdika?
segments.translation: One time me and my nephew were walking to the store. It was about a mile from the house. Somebody gave us a ride. It was our cousin, the Ketcher. “Would you all want some turnip?” he said. “Yeah, you mean turnip? And here it is winter.” I told him. When we got there he started digging and had a bunch of hay there, and underneath was the turnips. It looked like they had just grown, it was good. He gave those to us. They knew how to save things back then. They didn’t have to go get a freezer. Well, they couldn’t afford it, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎢᎦᏓᏅ Ꮭ ᏗᎾᎦᎵᏍ--ᏗᎾᎦᎵ--ᏗᎾᎦᎵᏍᎩ ᏱᏚᏂᎾᏁ ᏍᏊ ᎢᎦᏓ
segments.transliteration: igadanv tla dinagalis--dinagali--dinagalisgi yiduninane squu igada
segments.translation: They didn’t have electric back then either.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꭺ.ᎯᏴ ᏐᎢ ᏦᏍᏓᏝᎲᎳ ᎧᏁᎮᏍᎬ uh *gas* ᎠᏟᏍᏓ ᎠᏴᏜᏗᏍᏗᏍᎩ ᎤᏂᎭ ᎠᏗ ᎧᏃᎲᎳ ᏗᏖᏍᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᎠᏟᏍᏓ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏗ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ-- Ꮭ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ Ꮿ.ᏅᏓᏓ ᏂᎯ?
segments.transliteration: go.hiyv soi tsosdatlahvla kanehesgv uh *gas* atlisda ayvdladisdisgi uniha adi kanohvla ditesdinv squu sgiyusdi atlisda gehv adi tla gohusdi-- tla sgiyusdi ya.nvdada nihi?
segments.translation: While ago I was talking to someone, he was saying they used gas to cool their place. Also, for the iron, they used gas. But you don’t see that now. You all didn’t have anything like that?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: No?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ’Ᏺ ᏥᏙᎩᎲ ᎮᎾ uh...ᏗᏖᏍᏗ uh..*electric* ᏂᎨᎲᎾ ᏙᏳ, *stove*Ꭲ ᏱᏗᏣ,ᏢᏂ ᎤᏗᏞᎦ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ, ᏓᏂᏖᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ ... Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮤ ᏫᏂ,ᏚᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: ayadv’yo tsidogihv hena uh...ditesdi uh..*electric* nigehvna doyu, *stove*i yiditsa,tlvni uditlega yinuli,stana, danitesgv tsigehv ... tla yawana,ta wini,duli,stanv squu
segments.translation: Me. We had an iron. But you put them on top of the stove and got them hot. That’s how they ironed. I don’t know what became of them.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Where you used to live, what was it like?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: Uh...ᏭᎪᏛ ᎨᎲ uh...ᎯᎢ ᏥᏂ,ᎦᏛ. ᎦᏄᎳ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎥᎾᎾ ᏙᏣᏓᏏᏂ,ᏙᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏙᏣᏓᏍᎦᎸᏁᎲ ᏙᏱ ᎦᎵᏦᏕ ... ᎣᏍᏓ ᎢᎦ ᏓᎾᏁᎶᎲᏍᎬ “kick-the-can” ᏱᎩ, ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎲ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᏒᏛ’Ꮓ ᏱᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᎾ ᏍᎩᏛ’Ꮓ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᎪᏛ. ᎾᎥ Ᏻ,ᏯᎾ,ᏖᏏᏢ’Ꮓ ᏓᏂ--ᏓᎾ,ᏎᎯᎲ ᎥᎾᏛ ᎢᏤᏙᎭ Ꭹ.Ꮆ’Ꮓ ᏳᏯᎾ,ᏖᏏᏢ’Ꮓ ᏚᏲᏍᎬ’Ꮓ ᎡᎵᏭ’Ꮓ ᎤᎷᎶᏣ, ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎲ ᎯᎾ ᏃᏣᏛᏁᎲ ᏦᎦᏛ.Ꮢ Paul Cooksey Ꮎ ᎤᏥ--ᎤᏥ ᏦᏤᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏙᎦᏛ.Ꮢ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏥᏈᏍᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏣᎲ ᎣᎦᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏝᏍᎩᏂ, ᎤᏩᏌᏅ, ᏍᏊ ᎤᏂᎮ *T.V.* ᎥᎾ ᎣᏤᎬ ᏦᎦᎦ,Ꮩ.ᏍᏓᏁᎬ ᎣᏍᏓ *T.V.* ᎣᎦᎦ,Ꮩ.--ᏲᎦᏚᎵ ᎣᎩᎪᏛ.ᏙᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ’Ꭱ--ᎠᏯᏛ ᎣᏍᏓ’Ꭱ ᎨᎲ *I mean* Ꮭ--Ꮭ ᏯᎩ,ᏐᏃᏤ.Ꮂ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᏄᏓᎴ *T.V.* ᏧᎲ
segments.transliteration: Uh...wugodv gehv uh...hii tsini,gadv. ganula nigohilv vnana dotsadasini,dohv tsigehv dotsadasgalvnehv doyi galitsode ... osda iga dananelohvsgv “kick-the-can” yigi, tsana,dihv tsigehv usvdv’no yinuli,stana sgidv’no gi.lo godv. nav yu,yana,tesitlv’no dani--dana,sehihv vnadv itsedoha gi.lo’no yuyana,tesitlv’no duyosgv’no eliwu’no ululotsa, nigali,sdihv hina notsadvnehv tsogadv.sv Paul Cooksey na utsi--utsi tsotsehv vna dogadv.sv etsulaha tsiquisdv osda tsahv ogadvne,di tlasgini, uwasanv, squu unihe *T.V.* vna otsegv tsogaga,do.sdanegv osda *T.V.* ogaga,do.--yogaduli ogigodv.dodi osda’e--ayadv osda’e gehv *I mean* tla--tla yagi,sonotse.hv gi.lo nudale *T.V.* tsuhv
segments.translation: Most of all, the grass was tall all the time. And that’s where we crawled around playing hide-and-seek. They used to play kick-the-can. And when night came, and when somebody kicked their can close to the fire, they would count them. And when another kicked their’s to the fire, they were way over there, then we turned it loose. And we had to get out [of the game]. That’s what we were doing growing up. Paul Cooksey and his mom. That’s where we lived and we grew up with them. There were a lot of things to do. But they were the only ones that had a TV. And we went over there when we wanted to watch something. For me, it was okay for them to have a TV. I didn’t get mad about it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ Ꮭ Ꮩ’ Ꮶ--Ꮶ- ᎡᏚᏓ, ᎡᎵᏏᏅ, ᏱᎨᎮ Ᏺ’ ᏍᎩ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᏥᏙᏥᏪᎮ ᎨᎮ ᎠᏂᏁᎳᏅ ᏧᎦᎴᏛ ᎥᎾ ᏗᏢ Jim Bunch ᎥᎾ--ᎥᎾ ᏧᏂᎮ’Ᏺ ... ᏙᏓᏆᏍᎬ ᏫᏃᎦᏓᏝᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎥᎾ ᏳᏙᎩᏴᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏳᏓᎵᎭ ᎥᎾ ᏫᎦᎷᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ *T.V.* ᏯᏒᏂ,Ꭶ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎤᏗᏞᎩ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏗᎢ!” ᏦᎩᏍᏚᏁᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ... um...ᏂᎯᎾ? ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗᏓᏁ Ꮧ--Ꮧ--ᏗᏣᏛ.Ꮢ?
segments.transliteration: ayadv tla do’ tso--tso- eduda, elisinv, yigehe yo’ sgi sgina, tsidotsiwehe gehe aninelanv tsugaledv vna ditlv Jim Bunch vna--vna tsunihe’yo ... dodaquasgv winogadatlago tsigehv vna yudogiyvna tsigehv yudaliha vna wigalugv tsigehv *T.V.* yasvni,ga tsigehv “uditlegi nigali,sdii!” tsogisduneho tsigehv ... um...nihina? ‘do usdidane di--di--ditsadv.sv?
segments.translation: But us, our grandparents weren’t really our grandparents. We just called them that. They lived close by Tsugaledv… Jim Bunch. They had a TV though. We were gathered over there on Sundays, and they would come and get us there. Then they would come get us. Every once in a while, he would come and touch the TV, and he was telling us that it was getting too hot. And he would turn it off. What about you? What was it like as you grew up?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Uh… I don’t know what to say. [laughs] What?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Just tell what you saw.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Y’all used to go do laundry in town, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ uh... Ꭸ.ᏓᎵ’Ꮫ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎹ ᎨᎢ Salem-Ꭲ’Ꮲ ᏙᏨ,ᎩᎶᎥ ᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv uh... ge.dali’dv tsigehv ama gei Salem-i’tlv dotsv,gilov gehv gohiga tsigehv
segments.translation: Uh… There used to be water at the bottom of the hill. And that’s where we used to do laundry, a long time ago.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Just by the water.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎠᏯ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᎸ ᏙᏨ,ᎩᎶᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ ᎡᏅᎯ ᏩᎩ,ᏐᎯᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎠᎻᏃ ᎣᎦᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᎨᎢ ᎦᏄᎪᎬ ᏬᎵᏗ’Ꮫ ᏥᏚᏙᎥ ᎥᎾ ᎦᏁᎸ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv aya tsosdadalv dotsv,gilosgo gehv envhi wagi,sohisdi gehv amino ogaditasdi gei ganugogv wolidi’dv tsidudov vna ganelv tsigehv
segments.translation: Me and my sister were doing washing. We had to go way down the hill. And our drinking water was a spring, far off. Wol(i)didv was his name that was living there.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Who was it?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Wol(i)didv Advga.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: Walter Duncan Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮤ, ᎯᏲᎵᎦ, ᏱᎩ.
segments.transliteration: Walter Duncan tla yawana,ta, hiyoliga, yigi.
segments.translation: Walter Duncan, I don’t know if you know him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎾᏴ ᏬᏥᏁᎩᏍᎪ ᎠᎹ ᎣᎦᏗᏔᏍᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎾᎾ ᎣᎦᏓᏍᏓᏴᏙᏗ ᎨᎲ ᎥᎾᏴ ᎡᎳᏗ ᎤᏪᏴ ᏬᏥᏁᎩᏍᎪ
segments.transliteration: vnayv wotsinegisgo ama ogaditasdi gehv nana ogadasdayvdodi gehv vnayv eladi uweyv wotsinegisgo
segments.translation: We went and got our drinking [water] over there, but to cook, we went down to the creek.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏃᎦᏛᏁᎸ ᏍᏊ ᏙᏥᎾᏫᏙ ᎨᎲ ᎢᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏗᎦᏅᎪᎪ ᎣᏦᏎᎲ ᎨᎲ ᏗᎦᏅᎪᎬ ᏬᏥᎷᎬ ᎠᏃᏛ.ᏍᎬ’Ꮫ *pots*ᎢᏅ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ, ᏓᏅ--ᏧᏗᏞᎩ ᏓᏅᏁᎲ ᏓᏅ,ᎩᎶᏍᎬ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ ᏍᏊ ᎤᎾᎵᎪ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮎ Paul ᎤᏂᏥ ᎠᏯᏅ ᎣᎩᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎾ,ᏓᎸ’ᏪᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᏊ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎠᏎᏅ...ᎠᏎᏅ ᏄᏓᎴ...ᏄᏓᎴᏛᏒ Ꮎ ᏧᏂᏙᏓ, ᎨᎲ ᎨᏎ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏚᎾ,Ꮫ.Ꮢ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ... ᎠᎹᏯ ᏓᏅ,ᎩᎶᏍᎬ ᎡᏧᎳ,
segments.transliteration: ayadv squu utloyi nogadvnelv squu dotsinawido gehv inv squu diganvgogo otsosehv gehv diganvgogv wotsilugv anodv.sgv’dv *pots*inv tsuna,tana, danv--tsuditlegi danvnehv danv,gilosgv nigohilv’dv squu unaligo tsigehv na Paul unitsi ayanv ogitsi tsigehv dina,dalv’weyusdi squu gehv sginana asenv...asenv nudale...nudaledvsv na tsunidoda, gehv gese sginana duna,dv.sv etsulaha sginana ... amaya danv,gilosgv etsula,
segments.translation: We did the same, too. We took our clothes, and it was far, where the spring was. When we got there, they would build fires and they had those big pots. They made them hot. And that’s where they washed. Paul’s mom and our mom, they did that all the time. They were just like sisters. But they had different dads. They grew up together. They did their laundry at this water.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Were they just like a family?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᎾᎥ ᏃᎦᏛᏅ ᏭᏟ’ᎡᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᎬᏱ ᎡᎵᏭ uh... ᎡᎵᏭ uh... *half a—quarter mile*Ꮽ ᎴᏱᎦ, ᏗᏂᏁᎴ ᎨᏛ. ᏥᎦᏗ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎥᎾᏛ Ꮧ--Ꮲ ᏕᏴ’Ꮓ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏧᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏗᏩᏛ.Ꮂ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎠᏕᎳ Ꮎ ᎨᏛ. ᏥᎨᎲ ᏗᎬ,ᎩᎶᏍᎩ’Ꮫ ᎨᎲ ᏧᏓᏃᏴᏍᏙᏅ Ꮎ *motor* ᏥᎦᏝ ᏥᎨᎰ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᎩᎾᏛ Ꮎ “ᏗᏨ,ᎩᎶᏍᏗᏭ ᏱᏣᏚᎵ,” ᎠᏗ Ꭼ,ᏗᎰ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᎦᎵᏍᎪᎵᏓᏁᎰ ᎨᎲ ᎡᎵᏭᏛ ᎤᎾᎵ ᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯᏅ ᏥᎩ ᏙᎲ? ᎨᏍᏗ ᏱᏓᏃ,ᏙᎵ,Ꭶ, ᏏᏓᏁᎸᎧ? ᎨᏍᏗ’Ᏺ ᎠᏎᏅ ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ, ᎪᏪᎸᏅ ᎪᏪᎸ’ᏛᏍᏊ ᏙᎲ? ᏓᎾ,ᏓᎴᎨᏍᏗ ᎠᏗ ᏙᏳ,ᏅᏍᏊ ᏫᏥᎪᏩ,ᏘᎰ’Ꮫ ᏍᎩ ᏄᏍᏗᏓᏅ Ꮩ’...ᏙᏳ
segments.transliteration: vv nav nogadvnv wutli’edv tsigehv agvyi eliwu uh... eliwu uh... *half a—quarter mile*wu leyiga, dininele gedv. tsigadi sginana vnadv di--tlv deyv’no osda tsuli,stanidolv adela diwadv.hv sgina adela na gedv. tsigehv digv,gilosgi’dv gehv tsudanoyvsdonv na *motor* tsigatla tsigeho yusdi sginadv na “ditsv,gilosdiwu yitsaduli,” adi gv,diho tsigehv ogalisgolidaneho gehv eliwudv unali gehv gohiga tsigehv gohinv tsigi dohv? gesdi yidano,doli,ga, sidanelvka? gesdi’yo asenv yuli,sdodi nusdidanv, gowelvnv gowelv’dvsquu dohv? dana,dalegesdi adi doyu,nvsquu witsigowa,tiho’dv sgi nusdidanv do’...doyu
segments.translation: I guess. They grew up close neighbors. We all were really close. At first they lived about a half, quarter mile from Getv. Something happened. This Getv, they found some money and she started doing laundry in town. The kind that have motors in them. “You can go ahead and wash if y’all want to,” she was letting us do our laundry there, too. They used to be good friends back then. But today the families don’t get along, do they? I guess it’s happening like it’s supposed to, because that’s how it’s going to be, like in the Bible. They’re not going to be getting along, it says. And I do see it today.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᎾᎳᏡᏗᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᏗᏛ um... ᎡᎵᎲ...ᏲᎲ ᏯᏛᏁ,Ꮧ ᏓᏂᏍᏓᏲᎯᎲ ᏱᎩ *Thanksgiving* ᎴᏱᎦ Ᏺ’ ᏕᏣᏓᏟᏏᎮ?
segments.transliteration: analatludihesdi adidv um... elihv...yohv yadvne,di danisdayohihv yigi *Thanksgiving* leyiga yo’ detsadatlisihe?
segments.translation: They’re going to be spiteful to each other, it says. But when it was Christmas or Thanksgiving, your family would all gather together?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏥᎨᏒ’Ꮫ Ꮩ’ ᏙᏣᏓᏟᏏᏍᎬ uh...ᏳᏓᎭ ᎣᎩᏚᏥ, ᏧᏪᏅᏒ ᏬᏤᏙᎰ Ꮎ Henry Adair ᏧᏙᎢᏓ ᏗᎦᏁᎸ ᎢᏦᏗᏴ ᎥᎾ ᎣᏣᏂᎩᏍᎪ ᎨᎲ ᎣᎩᏒᎯᎲ ᏏᏛ ᏦᎪᎯᏳᏒ Santa Claus ᎾᎯᏳ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎦ)
segments.transliteration: vv tsigesv’dv do’ dotsadatlisisgv uh...yudaha ogidutsi, tsuwenvsv wotsedoho na Henry Adair tsudoida diganelv itsodiyv vna otsanigisgo gehv ogisvhihv sidv tsogohiyusv Santa Claus nahiyu (uyetsisga)
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s right. We all got together. Sometimes we went to my uncle’s house, Henry Adair where he lived. There in Itsodi. We walked that far to his house and spent the night. We still believed in Santa Claus then. [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᏯ’Ꭱ ᎢᎦ ᎦᏥᎶᎾᏍᏓ--ᎦᏥᎶᎾᏍᏓ ᏗᏂᏲᏟ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ,Ꮽ ᏍᎩ ᏥᎩ ᏌᏊ ᏔᎵ,ᏍᎪᎯ ᏳᏕᏘᏴᏓ ᏃᏊ ᎠᏂᏔᎵᏛ ᏗᎬᎩᎵᏏ ᏔᎵ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ Ꭿ’Ꭱ ᏂᎦᏥ--ᏂᎦᏥᏴᏁᎸ Ꮎ *tape recorders* ᏥᏓᎲ ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᎠᏯ ᎠᎩᎩᏒ ᎠᏩᏂᎩᏍᏔᏅ ᏞᎦ, ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᏂᏥᏬᏂᏍᎬᎾ ᎠᏩᏂᎩᏍᏔᏅ ‘ᎸᏢᏃ ᏧᏠᎦᎴᏓ, ᎤᏬᏂᎯᏍᏗ ᏩᎩᏬᏂᏒ ᏙᏳ,Ꮓ ᎣᎩᏢᏗ ᎬᎩᎪᎥ ᏫᎦᎵ--ᏫᎦᏂᏒᏍᎬ ᎬᎩᎪᎥ ᎤᎾᎾ,Ꮫ.Ꮫ ᏥᏅᎬ ... ᏃᏊ ᎣᏂ, ᏩᏮᏁᎳ Ꭺ.-- ᎡᏝᏪ ᎤᏂ-- Ꭺ.ᎯᏃ Ꮣ--ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏛᏳᎴᏅᎲ ᎬᎩᎪᏩᏘᎲ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ Ꮟ Ꭺ.Ꭿ ᏥᎩ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᏂᏓ, ᎠᏂᏧᏣ, ᏕᏥ-- ᎮᏍᏗ ᏳᎾᎾ,Ꮤ ᏍᎩ ᏂᎦᏥᏴᏁᎸ-- Ꮟ ᎤᏃᎯᏳ ᏧᏠᎦᎴᏓ, ᎤᏪᏙᎴ
segments.transliteration: aya’e iga gatsilonasda--gatsilonasda diniyotli tsuna,tana,wu sgi tsigi saquu tali,sgohi yudetiyvda noquu anitalidv digvgilisi tali, anitsutsa hi’e nigatsi--nigatsiyvnelv na *tape recorders* tsidahv sgi’e aya agigisv awanigistanv tlega, gohusdi, nitsiwonisgvna awanigistanv ‘lvtlvno tsutlogaleda, uwonihisdi wagiwonisv doyu,no ogitlvdi gvgigov wigali--wiganisvsgv gvgigov unana,dv.dv tsinvgv ... noquu oni, wawvnela go.-- etlawe uni-- go.hino da--gawonisgv dvyulenvhv gvgigowatihv nigehvna si go.hi tsigi tsuna,tanida, anitsutsa, detsi-- hesdi yunana,ta sgi nigatsiyvnelv-- si unohiyu tsutlogaleda, uwedole
segments.translation: Me. I really got the kids tricked. Even the grown ones, one is 20 years old. Two of my grandkids are boys. This is what I did to them, when there were tape recorders. I got one, one time, I turned it on but didn’t say anything. After a while, I talked like Santa Claus. When we went to bed they saw me going to bed. They knew I was in bed and I turned it on and it started playing but they knew I was in bed. Even today the older boys still don’t know I did that. They still believe that Santa Claus came.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: They still believe it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: But I really tricked them.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎠᏯᏛ ᎪᎯᏗ ᏦᎪᎯᏳᏒ Santa Claus-Ꭲ ‘ᏢᏴ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ “ᎦᏙ ᎣᏂ,Ᏼ--ᎣᏂ,Ᏼ ᏓᏂᏅ,Ꭼ uh...ᎣᏥᏅ,ᏝᎥ ‘ᏙᎲ ᏍᎩ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎣᎨᏥᎥᏌ?” ᎾᏅ, ᎠᏯ ᎪᏍᏗ, ᎰᏩ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ ᎠᏪᎵᏒ ᎩᎳ ᎠᏯ ᎠᏩᏕᎳᎰᏒ’Ꮓ uh...Santa Claus-Ꮓ ᏝᏃ ᏱᎨᎮ (ᎤᏰᏥᏍᎦ) ᎾᎮᎾ Ꮎ ᎡᏚᏥ ᎮᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎣᏍᏓ Ꮎ ᎠᏩᏘᏍᎩ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏕᎳ Ꮎ ᎠᏥᎳ ᏅᏃᎯ ᏧᎸᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏂᎪᎯᎸ’Ꮫ Ꮎ *bicycle* ᏯᏥᏁ Ꮎ ᎤᏪᏥ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎠᏯ Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏲᏥᎪᏩᏘᎮ ᎠᏎᏃ, ‘Ꮲ...ᏯᏩᏓᏅ,ᏖᏝ ᎣᎩᏥ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎪᎯ--ᎪᎯᏗ ᎮᎾ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏙᎦᏛ.ᎯᏍᏔᏅ Ꮭ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏯᏩᏛ.Ꭾ ᏄᏓᎴ ᎠᏕᎳ ᏍᎩᏭ ᎢᎦ *welfare* ᏥᏚᏙᎥ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ...ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏙᎦ--ᏙᎦᏛ.Ꮢ...ᏃᏊ, ᏁᎲᎾ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎣᎩᏙᏓ Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎣᎩᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏩᎧ ᎮᎾ, ᏚᎾᏝᎥ’Ᏺ...uh...ᏍᎩᏭᏅ,...Ꮟ ᏄᏲᎱᏒᎾ’Ᏺ Ꮪ--ᏚᎾ,ᏕᏐᏅ ᎤᎾ,Ꮫ.ᏛᎲ ᏂᎦᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎾᏅᎦ ᎨᎲ ᏩᎦ,
segments.transliteration: ayadv gohidi tsogohiyusv Santa Claus-i ‘tlvyv awadelahosv “gado oni,yv--oni,yv daninv,gv uh...otsinv,tlav ‘dohv sgi osda ogetsivsa?” nanv, aya gosdi, howa nigehvna awelisv gila aya awadelahosv’no uh...Santa Claus-no tlano yigehe (uyetsisga) nahena na edutsi hena tsigehv osda na awatisgi gehv adela na atsila nvnohi tsulvsdanehv gehv sgina nigohilv’dv na *bicycle* yatsine na uwetsi atsutsa aya tla osda yotsigowatihe aseno, ‘tlv...yawadanv,tetla ogitsi tsigehv gohi--gohidi hena uwasa dogadv.histanv tla osda yawadv.he nudale adela sgiwu iga *welfare* tsidudov nahiyu tsigehv sgiyusdi...sgiyusdi doga--dogadv.sv...noquu, nehvna nuli,stanv ogidoda na’e ogidoda tsigehv waka hena, dunatlav’yo...uh...sgiwunv,...si nuyohusvna’yo du--duna,desonv una,dv.dvhv nigali,stanv nanvga gehv waga,
segments.translation: We believed in Santa Claus for a long time. One time I realized. We were in bed near our parents, but somehow the others got a better present than me. That’s when I found there wasn’t any Santa Claus. My uncle he always had money because he worked on the railroad. He always bought his son a bicycle. And we didn’t see anything. But when I think about it, my mom raised us and she hardly ever found money. Except they called it welfare—that’s all the money she got, after our dad passed. But our dad had cows. Before he died he sold them all. I guess he knew they wouldn’t know what to do with the cows.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᎠᎦ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᎤᏙᏓ ᏍᏊ ᎮᎾ ᎡᏧ--ᎡᏧᎵᎭ ᏙᏍᏗᎾᏝᎥ ‘ᏢᏴ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏍᏓᏱᏛ ᏱᏂ,ᎦᎵᏍᏗᏃᏛ ᏙᏍᏗᏯᏍᎬᏃ ᎢᎦ ᏴᏍᏕᎵ,ᏙᏗ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: nadv aga,sdayvhvsgi udoda squu hena etsu--etsuliha dosdinatlav ‘tlvyv tsigehv sdayidv yini,galisdinodv dosdiyasgvno iga yvsdeli,dodi gehv
segments.translation: My wife’s dad had cows, too. I think, once, we both had cows together. When it got to be hard times, we would put one cow in the truck. We could really depend on it.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ! ᎾᎯᏳ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏯᏛ ᎡᏙᏓ ᏥᏕᎦᏂᏕᎬ ᏍᎪᎯᏥᏊᏭ ᏥᏕᎦᏂᏕᎪ ᏩᎧ ᏧᎾ,ᏔᎾ Ꭺ.ᎯᏅ ᏥᎩ ᎠᎦᏴᎵ ᎾᎥ
segments.transliteration: vv! nahiyu tsigehv ayadv edoda tsideganidegv sgohitsiquuwu tsideganidego waka tsuna,tana go.hinv tsigi agayvli nav
segments.translation: Yeah! Well back then, when my dad was selling his cows. He just sold them for $100, the grown ones. But today, it’s almost $1,000.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎠᎦᏴᎵ ᎾᎥ ᎠᎾ,ᏈᏱ...*yeah.* ᎤᏟᏍᏗᎢ’Ꭱ ᏓᎩ--ᏓᎩᏂ--ᏓᎩᏂ,ᏗᏅ ᎠᏯ ᏗᏩᏤᎵ ... ᎾᎿ uh...Ꭿ-Ꭿ- Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, Ꮿ.Ꮕ,ᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᏣᏙᏓ ᏨᏥᎴᏱᎦ ᎨᏒ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ, ᎧᏁᏍᎨ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ ᎠᎴ--...Ꮭ ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ Ꮿ.Ꮕ,ᏓᏗᏍᎪ ᎦᏣᏃᎮᏗ ᎨᎲ?
segments.transliteration: agayvli nav ana,quiyi...*yeah.* utlisdii’e dagi--dagini--dagini,dinv aya diwatseli ... nahna uh...hi-hi- tla gohusdi, ya.nv,dadisgo tsadoda tsvtsileyiga gesv gohusdi, kanesge nuli,stanidolv ale--...tla sgiyusdi ya.nv,dadisgo gatsanohedi gehv?
segments.translation: Yeah, they’re paying $1,000. I sold mine too quick. …What about? You don’t remember your dad or mom telling anything that happened? You don’t remember anything that you can tell?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: Huh uh. Ꮭ’Ᏺ...uh ᏍᎩᏭᏂᎦ Ꮎ ᏥᎦᏃᎭᎵᏙᎲ ᏧᏟ ᏚᏲᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎣᎩᏙᏓ ᏥᎨᎲ ‘Ꮲ ‘ᎸᏢᏴ ᎤᏨᏓᏆᏛ ᏒᎾᎴᎢᏃ ᏱᏓᎢ ᏥᎨᎲᏃ Ꮭ’Ᏺ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏱᏫ,ᎦᏃᎭᎵᏙᎲ ᎾᎮᎾ Ꮎ ᎤᏪᏥ Ꭰ-- ᎤᏪᏥ ᎠᏧᏣ ᎤᎾᎵᎪᏎ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏰᏟ ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏝ uh...ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏝᏍᏊ ᏯᏩᎾᏔ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᏱᏓᏂᎯ ᎨᎲ ᏧᏟ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎩᏟ ᏚᏂᎾᏝᎥ’Ᏺ *hounds*’Ᏺ’Ꮩ’ ᏧᏟ ᎤᏂᏲᎲ ᏚᎾᏛ.ᏓᏍᏗᏭ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏂᏰᎸᏒ
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. tla’yo...uh sgiwuniga na tsiganohalidohv tsutli duyohv aya ogidoda tsigehv ‘tlv ‘lvtlvyv utsvdaquadv svnaleino yidai tsigehvno tla’yo uwasa yiwi,ganohalidohv nahena na uwetsi a-- uwetsi atsutsa unaligose gehv ayetli otsatlanvtla uh...sginana tlasquu yawanata ilvhiyu yidanihi gehv tsutli sgihena yusdi gitli duninatlav’yo *hounds*’yo’do’ tsutli uniyohv dunadv.dasdiwu osda uniyelvsv
segments.translation: Uh uh. Not really. Except, my dad was hunting, looking for foxes. Sometimes he would be all night and come home early in the morning. And he wasn’t hunting alone. His son, my half-brother, would go with him. I don’t know if they killed any foxes. They had hound dogs that would hunt foxes. They just liked to listen to them. [laughs]

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏓ,Ꮫ ᏍᎩᎡ ᏯᏛᏁᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏚᎾᏝᎥ ᏍᏊ ᎩᏟ
segments.transliteration: edoda,dv sgie yadvnetsigehv tsidunatlav squu gitli
segments.translation: My dad used to do that, too. He had dogs.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: There used to be a lot of people that did that.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮤ ᎯᏯᏅᏓᏗ “ᏥᎩᎵ” ᏣᏃᎮᎲ Lee Bunch ᏍᎩ’Ꭱ ᏯᏁᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: tla yawana,ta hiyanvdadi “tsigili” tsanohehv Lee Bunch sgi’e yanena tsigehv
segments.translation: That guy Tsigili, Lee Bunch, I don’t know if you remember him. He used to go with him.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Really?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah. They would spend the night.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: I had seen him before, Tsigili [that was].

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Did you have brothers?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: How many?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: Uh...ᎠᏂᏔᎵ ᏧᏂᏲᎱᏒᏃ Ꮎ ᎦᎵᏉᎩ’Ꮫ ᎠᏁᎮ...ᎠᏁᎯ ᎣᏤᎵ
segments.transliteration: Uh...anitali tsuniyohusvno na galiquogi’dv anehe...anehi otseli
segments.translation: Two of them are already gone. There are seven still here. We think.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏍ ᏍᏊ Ꭿ’ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏦᏍᏗᏃᎮᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᏍ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏍᏊ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎵᎮ ᏙᏧᎾ,Ꮫ.ᏏᏗᎮ?
segments.transliteration: sgis squu hi’ yusdi tsosdinohesgv sgis yusdi squu nanadvnelihe dotsuna,dv.sidihe?
segments.translation: This stuff we’re talking about did they do anything like that, too, as they were growing up?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: What is it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꮎ Ꭿ’ Jerry ᏦᏍᏗᏃᎮ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏧᎶᏒ ᏍᎩ ᏍᏊ ᎤᏠᏱ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎾᎾᏛᏁᎮ?
segments.transliteration: na hi’ Jerry tsosdinohe yusdi tsulosv sgi squu utloyi yusdi nanadvnehe?
segments.translation: What me and Jerry were talking about. Did they do the same thing too?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They were hunting?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mm-hmm.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They were fishing --

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏓ,Ꮫ ᎠᏂ--ᎠᏂᏧᏣ ᎨᎲ’Ᏺ Ꮭ ᏍᎩ ᏄᎾ,ᏛᏁᎸ ᏱᎩ ᎣᏣᏝᏅᏝ
segments.transliteration: edoda,dv ani--anitsutsa gehv’yo tla sgi nuna,dvnelv yigi otsatlanvtla
segments.translation: My dad, except the boys, they didn’t do that. My siblings.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They didn’t?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Huh…

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᎡᏙᏓ ᎮᎾ ᎤᏩᏌ ᏥᏚᏲᎲ ᏥᏍᏚ ᎥᏅᏥ ᏱᎩ
segments.transliteration: edoda hena uwasa tsiduyohv tsisdu vnvtsi yigi
segments.translation: Except my dad, he would hunt for rabbits when it snowed.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And then you all cooked them?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mm-hmm. Me and Mom.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I really like rabbit meat.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Me too.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏌᎶᎵ ᏃᏭ Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏗᎬᏙᏗ ᏱᎩ
segments.transliteration: saloli nowu tla gohusdi digvdodi yigi
segments.translation: I don’t have any use for squirrel. I don’t like them.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: But we made squirrel dumplings.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Oh!

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᏥᏍᏚ ᏣᏂᏒᏂ,Ꮫ.ᏍᎬᏅ ᎥᎥ...huh uh, ᏣᎾ--ᏣᎾᎵᏟ,ᏗᎲᏛ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎠᎹ ᎠᏟᏍᏛ ᎠᏃᏢᏍᎬ ᏃᏊ ᏥᏩᏂᏒᏂ,Ꮫ,ᏍᎬ ᏥᏍᏚ ᎠᎵᏟ,ᏔᏅ
segments.transliteration: tsisdu tsanisvni,dv.sgvnv vv...huh uh, tsana--tsanalitli,dihvdv agvyi nuli,stanv ama atlisdv anotlvsgv noquu tsiwanisvni,dv,sgv tsisdu alitli,tanv
segments.translation: And roasted rabbit. They would boil the meat first, and then roast it. And then they would make gravy.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Is it flour?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ Ꮎ ᎠᎵᏟ,ᏔᏅ Ꮎ ᎭᏫᏯ ᏥᏍᏚ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏣᏅ,ᏗᎲ Ꮎ ᎠᎹ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎾᏑᏍᏗ ᎤᏖᏗᏛ ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: vv na alitli,tanv na hawiya tsisdu sgina tsanv,dihv na ama gehv unasusdi utedidv tsigehv
segments.translation: They used broth where they had boiled the meat, to make gravy. And it was really good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: It really was.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: “I really want it,” I tell him. Cause I get hungry for that.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: But he doesn’t kill the rabbit?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: Huh uh. Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᏯᏩᏘᎰ... Ꮭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᎬᏛᎦ
segments.transliteration: Huh uh. tla gohusdi yawatiho... tla gohusdi osda yigvdvga
segments.translation: Uh uh. He doesn’t find them. He can’t do anything right.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎨᏍᏗ--ᎨᏍᏗᏅ ᏍᏊᏛᏃ ᎩᎶᏃ ᏱᎦᏃᎭᎵᏙᎯᏃ ᏥᏍᏚ ᏙᎧ?
segments.transliteration: gesdi--gesdinv squudvno gilono yiganohalidohino tsisdu doka?
segments.translation: But today, there’s hardly anybody that hunts rabbit.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Nobody knows how to do things like that anymore.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏳᏓᎭ ᎮᎾ... ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,Ꮣ ᏦᏨ,Ꮫ.ᎩᎶᏍᎬ ᎤᎷᏨ Moe Sawney ᏣᏃᏎᎲ “ᏥᏍᏚ ᏥᎷᎦ,” ᎤᏛᏅ ᎪᎳ ᏍᏊ ᎨᎲ *December*Ꮲ ᎧᎸ ᎤᏴᏟ “ᏙᏳ Ꮳ,ᏍᎦᏍᏗ ᏓᏥᏯᏯᎢ ᎠᏇᎵᏒ ᏫᏥᎷᏨ,” ᏧᏛᏅᏛ “ᎣᏍᏓ ᏂᏥᏴᏁᎲ ᏥᏁᎦᎵᎲ ᏥᎪᏱ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎤᏂᏅᎪᏨ!” ᏣᏗ ᏭᏟ ᏥᏭᏓᎢᏅᎡ ᎤᏍᏓᎦᏴᎯᏓ ᏗᎦᎾ ᏣᏗ
segments.transliteration: yudaha hena... saquu yuwaga,da tsotsv,dv.gilosgv ulutsv Moe Sawney tsanosehv “tsisdu tsiluga,” udvnv gola squu gehv *December*tlv kalv uyvtli “doyu tsa,sgasdi datsiyayai aquelisv witsilutsv,” tsudvnvdv “osda nitsiyvnehv tsinegalihv tsigoyi tsiquisdi uninvgotsv!” tsadi wutli tsiwudainve usdagayvhida digana tsadi
segments.translation: One time, we were washing, that Moe Sawney came. “I killed a rabbit,” he said. It was winter time, about December. It was really cold. “I thought I was going to eat the rabbit. When I got home,” he said. “I even skinned it. A bunch of bugs came out after I skinned it. So I just threw it away,” he said. It was laying there all frozen.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: *Yeah* ᎠᏯᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎩᏃᎭᎵᏙ ᏍᎩ ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏅ ᎢᎦᏓ ᏥᎪᏱ ᎬᏩᏂᏯᎥ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: *Yeah* ayadv squu aginohalido sgi nuli,stanv igada tsigoyi gvwaniyav gehv
segments.translation: Me too. When I hunted them too, some of them had bugs.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Rarely that happens.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᏝᏍ ᎤᏯ.Ꮫ.Ꮲ Ꭹ.Ꮃ, ᎠᏃᏍᏓ ᏯᎾᏗᎮ Ꮎ ᏥᏍᏚ
segments.transliteration: tlas uya.dv.tlv gi.la, anosda yanadihe na tsisdu
segments.translation: Don’t they say they’re not good until it frosts? After it frosts?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Frost.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: If it frosts.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I haven’t heard that before.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: No?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Uh uh.

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᏳᏂᏪᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ “ᎤᏯ.Ꮫ.Ꮲ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ᎠᏃᏍᏓ ᎨᎰ ᏍᎩᎾ Ꮭ ᏥᎪᏱ ᏱᎬᏩᏂᏯᎣ.”
segments.transliteration: sgi yuniwesdi tsigehv “uya.dv.tlv gi.la anosda geho sgina tla tsigoyi yigvwaniyao.”
segments.translation: That’s what they would say back then. “They’re not good until after it frosts. Bugs won’t be in them,” they used to say.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏥᏈᏍᏛ ᏍᎩᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏳᏂᏪᏍᏗ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎾᎿ ᎤᏂᎿᏑᎦ ᏥᏓ-
segments.transliteration: tsiquisdv sgina yusdi yuniwesdi tsigehv nahna unihnasuga tsida-
segments.translation: There were a lot of them that used to say that.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: it’s the same ain’t it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎤᏯ.Ꮫ.Ꮲ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ... ᏒᎩ ᎢᎾᎨᎢ ᎡᎯ, ᎢᏥᎩᏍᎩᏍ ᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᏯ.Ꮫ.Ꮲ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ...
segments.transliteration: uya.dv.tlv gi.la ... svgi inagei ehi, itsigisgis gehe nahiyu uya.dv.tlv gi.la ... svgi inagei ehi, itsigisgis gehe nahiyu?
segments.translation: Or when the possum grapes grew, they weren’t good until after the frost…

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Mary says something that is not transcribed

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏒᎩ ᎢᎾᎨᎢ ᎡᎯ, ᎢᏥᎩᏍᎩᏍ ᎨᎮ ᎾᎯᏳ?
segments.transliteration: svgi inagei ehi, itsigisgis gehe nahiyu?
segments.translation: Did you all eat wild onion back then?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yeah. When we made up our mind to go and get it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎠᏓᏁᎸ ᎠᏭᏴ ᏥᏄᏍᏛ ᎯᎸᏍᎩ ᎢᎦ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎣᎩᏂᎬ
segments.transliteration: sgidv nusdv adanelv awuyv tsinusdv hilvsgi iga osda oginigv
segments.translation: That’s the way it was at the house. There was several close to my house. We ate it all the time.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ ᏍᏊ ᏄᏍᏛ Rocky Mt. ᏗᏢ ᏥᏗᎨᎥ ᏍᎩᏭ ᏱᎦᏖᎾ Ꮻ.ᎷᎬ ᏱᎩ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎢᎦ Ᏹ.ᏩᏔ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sgidv squu nusdv Rocky Mt. ditlv tsidigev sgiwu yigatena wi.lugv yigi osda iga yi.wata gehv
segments.translation: Yeah, it was that way too, when we lived at Rocky Mount. You would just walk a little ways and find it.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏒᎯ ᏥᏩᎩᎦ,ᏛᏅ ‘Ꮲ ᏯᏩᏅᏔ Ꮎ ᏥᏓᏴ.ᏝᏗ ... ᏂᎯᎨ.’Ᏺ ᏒᎩ ᎢᎾᎨᎢ ᎡᎯ, ᎢᏥᎩᏍᎩ ᎨᎮ?
segments.transliteration: svhi tsiwagiga,dvnv ‘tlv yawanvta na tsidayv.tladi ... nihige.’yo svgi inagei ehi, itsigisgi gehe?
segments.translation: I went to check on it yesterday. But I don’t know because it’s too cold. How about you? Did y’all eat wild onion too?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: And poke salad?

segments.speaker: mary-scott
segments.text: ᎥᎥ ᏜᏱᏕ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏗ ᎠᏯ ᏌᏊ ᎣᏍᏗᎩᏍᎪ ᏳᏛᏁᏗ ᎤᏍᏗ ᏧᎦᎶᎦ ᎤᏩᏌ ᎠᎩᎸᏉᏗ
segments.transliteration: vv dlayide agilvquodi aya saquu osdigisgo yudvnedi usdi tsugaloga uwasa agilvquodi
segments.translation: Mm-hmm. I like poke salad. But we probably eat it just once and I like the smaller leaves.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Biscuits and gravy.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎾᏛ ᎠᏯ ᏗᏩᏛ.Ꮢ ᏗᏢ ᎨᎲ ᎤᎶᎨᏓᏭ ᏣᏂᎦ ᏥᎨᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮤ ᏚᏙᎥ ᏲᏁᎦ Ꭿ’Ꭱ ᏱᎦᏘ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᏍᎬ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎤᎶᎨᏓ ᏣᏃᏎᎲ ᏣᎳᎩ ᎬᏗ ᏍᎩᎾ ᎤᏖᏗ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏎᏅ ᏐᎢ ᏍᏊ ᎠᎾᏑᏴᏍᎬ ᏍᏊ ᏒᎩ--ᏒᎩ ᎢᎾᎨᎢ ᎡᎯ, ᏥᎩ, ᏓᎾ,--ᎡᏧᎳ ᏓᏅᏂᏍᏗᎲ ᎡᏧᎳᎭ ᎣᏏᏅ ᏥᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ ᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: nadv aya diwadv.sv ditlv gehv ulogedawu tsaniga tsigehv tla yawana,ta dudov yonega hi’e yigati nigalisdisgv tsigehv ulogeda tsanosehv tsalagi gvdi sgina utedi squu asenv soi squu anasuyvsgv squu svgi--svgi inagei ehi, tsigi, dana,--etsula danvnisdihv etsulaha osinv tsigehv aya gehv
segments.translation: But where I grew up they ate uloged(a). I don’t know what to call it in English. It used to grow about this [gestures] tall. And they called it Uloged(a) in Cherokee. It was good, too. But they would cook wild onion and uloged(a) together, and that was good.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: What is it, uloged(a)?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎤᎶᎨᏓ ᏚᏙᎥ ᎥᎥ Ꭿ’Ꭱ ᏂᎦᏘ ᏂᎦᎵᏍᏗᎲ ᏍᏘᎩᏓ ᏜᏱᏕ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ Ꮭ ᏜᏱᏕ ᏱᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: ulogeda dudov vv hi’e nigati nigalisdihv stigida dlayide iyusdi tla dlayide yigehv
segments.translation: Uloged(a) is its name. It grew about this [gestures] tall. And it’s almost like dlayide (poke salad), but it wasn’t.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᎪᏪᎵ ᎪᎱᏍᏗ ᎠᏤ ᏯᏩᏕᎶᏆ ... JerryᏃ ᏍᎩᏃᎯᏏ ᏄᏍᏛ...ᏄᎵ,ᏍᏔᏂᏙᎸ’Ꮥ ᏥᏕᏣᏓᏲᏎ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏤᏣ,ᏍᏕᎸ ‘Ꮩ ᎤᏍᏗᏕᎨ
segments.transliteration: goweli gohusdi atse yawadeloqua ... Jerryno sginohisi nusdv...nuli,stanidolv’de tsidetsadayose nahiyu tsetsa,sdelv ‘do usdidege
segments.translation: When I learn something new, I write it down. Jerry, tell me, about the time you got saved. What really happened?

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: You mean at the church?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: Ꭳ...ᎨᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᏱᏓᏭᎪᏕ ᏩᏴᎯᏍᏗ Ꮩ’ ᎮᎾ ᎦᎸᏉᏗᏳ ᎠᎢᏎᏒᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎦᎸᏉᏗ ᎠᏓᏅᏙᎯ ᏣᎾᏗᎰ John Jr. ᏥᎨᏒ ᎠᎵ,ᏣᏙᎲᏍᎬ ᎢᎾ ᎤᏍᏗ ᎠᏧᏣ ᏥᏂᏙᎲ...ᎠᏪᏅᏒ ᏣᎾ,ᏔᏍ...ᎠᏪᏅᏒ ᏓᏩᎴᏅᏓ ᎨᏍᏗ’Ꭱ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮫ ᏩᎩᎷᏨ ᎠᎬᏱ ᏗᏢ ᎩᎳ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᎥᎩᏯᏅᏅ ᎠᏧᏣ Ꮵ--ᏥᏯᏘᏅᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ SalemᎢ ᎮᎾ ᏥᎨᎲ ᏥᏓᏩᏓᏲᏒ ᎾᎯᏳ ... ᏙᏳ ᎮᎾ ᏣᏎᎦ--ᏍᎩᎧ Ꮒ,ᎬᏪ? ᏣᏎᎯᎮᏍᏗ Ꮎ “ᏖᎨᏍᏗ ᎮᏍᏗ Ᏹ.ᏍᏓᏅᏗᎮᏍᏗ ᎠᏗᏅ’Ꭷ ᏃᏊᎴ ‘ᎸᏢ ᎤᏣᏘᏅ ᏫᎪᏪᎳ “ᎾᏂᎥᏭ *or* ᏍᎩᏭ ᎨᎲ ᎦᎷᎬ Ꮭ ᏱᎦᏥᏓᎢᎬ,” ᏩᏗ ᏃᏊᎴ ᏍᏊ ᏙᎲ? ᏍᏊ ᏃᏊᎴ
segments.transliteration: o...gesdi’e yidawugode wayvhisdi do’ hena galvquodiyu aisesvhv nahiyu galvquodi adanvdohi tsanadiho John Jr. tsigesv ali,tsadohvsgv ina usdi atsutsa tsinidohv...awenvsv tsana,tas...awenvsv dawalenvda gesdi’e yawana,dv wagilutsv agvyi ditlv gila iyusdi vgiyanvnv atsutsa tsi--tsiyatinvhv nahiyu Salemi hena tsigehv tsidawadayosv nahiyu ... doyu hena tsasega--sgika ni,gvwe? tsasehihesdi na “tegesdi hesdi yi.sdanvdihesdi adinv’ka noquule ‘lvtlv utsatinv wigowela “nanivwu *or* sgiwu gehv galugv tla yigatsidaigv,” wadi noquule squu dohv? squu noquule
segments.translation: I didn’t really want to go. Holy Spirit got ahold of me. John Jr. was preaching. I had a little boy with me, when I went to the front. You know, I don’t remember getting up and walking to the front. Somebody took the little boy from me. It was at Salem when I got saved. Yidvsaga, is that what you say? That’s what it also says, ain’t it? It says, “Come on, don’t be stubborn, to come by yourself.” And then the Bible says, “If there are a lot, I will not turn them away,” ain’t it?

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: But it says, “He’s withdrawing.”

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎾᏛᎧ...ᎾᏛᎧ ᎠᎵᏣᏙᎲᏍᎬ ᏍᎩᏛ’Ꭷ ᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎮ ᏙᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᏊ
segments.transliteration: nadvka...nadvka alitsadohvsgv sgidv’ka dulvwisdanehe dohv nahiyu squu
segments.translation: Ain’t it, His preaching. That’s what is working on Him.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: ᏍᎩ ᏥᏚᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ ᎾᎯᏳ’Ꭱ ᎠᎦᏎᏏ ᏃᏊ ᎠᏥᎵᏅᏓᏕ ᏍᎩᏭᏅ ᎨᎲᎾ ᏯᎦᏎᏏ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ ᏍᏊ ᏱᎦ ᏱᏭᏓᎷᏤ
segments.transliteration: sgi tsidulvwisdanehv nahiyu’e agasesi noquu atsilinvdade sgiwunv gehvna yagasesi gayu,la squu yiga yiwudalutse
segments.translation: Yeah, while He’s working, that’s when He’s being withdrawn. Making room for Him. They can really be withdrawn, no matter who it is, when they get saved.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏙᏳ,Ꭷ ... ᎠᏯ ᎪᎵᎬ ᎨᎲ Ᏹ.ᏍᏓᏔᏅ ᏛᏓᏅᏏᎢ ᎤᏣᏘᏅ ᏓᎦᎶᏏ ᏐᎢ ᏧᏬᏢ ᏴᏫ, ᎾᎯᏳ ᏓᏂᎳᏫᎨ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ...Ꮭ ᎮᎾ ᏱᏓᏣ,ᏘᏰᏔᏂ ᏙᏳ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏣᎷᏨ ᎦᏳ,Ꮃ ᎮᎾ ᏂᎦᏓ ᏤᏅᏍᏗᏭ Ᏹ.ᏍᏓᏔᏅ’Ꮓ ᎪᎯᏗ ᎮᎾ’Ᏼ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮤ ‘Ᏼ ᏍᏊ ᎮᎾ Ꮑ.ᎲᎾ ᏱᎩ ᏙᏳ ᏃᏊᎴ Ꭹ.Ꮃ ... ᎤᏎᎩᏛ ᎾᏛᏁᎲ ᎦᎸᏉᏗ ᎠᏓᏅᏙᎯ ᎡᏙᎰ *y’know.*
segments.transliteration: doyu,ka ... aya goligv gehv yi.sdatanv dvdanvsii utsatinv dagalosi soi tsuwotlv yvwi, nahiyu danilawige tla hena...tla hena yidatsa,tiyetani doyu sginana nahiyu tsalutsv gayu,la hena nigada tsenvsdiwu yi.sdatanv’no gohidi hena’yv tla yawana,ta ‘yv squu hena ne.hvna yigi doyu noquule gi.la ... usegidv nadvnehv galvquodi adanvdohi edoho *y’know.*
segments.translation: The way I understand it, if you make it hard on Him, He’s gonna move to somebody else. While they are having church, they’re not going to beg you. It is just up to you to get up and go. If you make it hard on Him it’ll be a long time… You might not even be alive then. But the Lord’s will moves in mysterious ways. As we move about.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Sometimes it is hard to let go of the world.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Very… Very.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: That’s how they are today.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: That’s right.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: They don’t want --

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛ’Ꭷ...ᏍᎩᏛ’Ꭷ Ꮎ ᎡᎶᎯ ᏍᏓᏱ’Ꭱ ᏚᏩᏅᏕᎬ ‘ᎸᏍᎩᏛ ᏥᎵᏃᎮᏗᎲ ᎠᏧᏣ “ᎿᏛᏅ ᏥᎩ,” ᏥᏲᏎᎮ “ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎩ Ᏹ.Ꮿ ‘ᎸᏢ ᎩᎳᏃ Ꮎ *flashlight* Ᏹ.ᏨᏍᏔᏅ ᎢᎦ ᏱᏥᏎᎪᎨ Ꮎ ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎬ” ᏥᏲᏎᎲ ᎤᏠᏱᏪ...ᎤᏠᏱᏪ ᎢᎸᎯᏳ ᎤᏬᎯᏳ ᏂᎨᎲᎾ ᏥᎩ ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎩ ᎾᎬᏅ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ Ꮎ ᏃᏊ...ᏧᏁᎵᏗ ᏳᎷᏨ ᏥᏌ ᏚᏙᏍᏛ ᏳᏔᏅ ᎠᎾ ᎠᏓᏅᏍᏗ ᏎᏔᏂ ᏝᏃ ᏳᏚᎵ ᎤᏴᏍᏗ ᎥᎾ’Ꭱ ᎤᏝᏅᏓᏃ ᎣᏍᏓ ᎤᏬᎯᏳᏗ ᎢᏳᏃ ᏓᎪᎯᏳᏂ ᏄᎨᏳᎲᏍᎬᎾ, ᏱᎩ, ᎡᎶᎯ ᏄᏍᏛ ᎾᎿᏃ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮤ ᎯᏲᎵᎦ, ᏱᎩ, Dave Sanders ᏥᎨᎲ
segments.transliteration: sgidv’ka...sgidv’ka na elohi sdayi’e duwanvdegv ‘lvsgidv tsilinohedihv atsutsa “hnadvnv tsigi,” tsiyosehe “uli,sigi yi.ya ‘lvtlv gilano na *flashlight* yi.tsvstanv iga yitsisegoge na uli,sigv” tsiyosehv utloyiwe...utloyiwe ilvhiyu uwohiyu nigehvna tsigi uli,sigi nagvnv sginana na noquu...tsunelidi yulutsv tsisa dudosdv yutanv ana adanvsdi setani tlano yuduli uyvsdi vna’e utlanvdano osda uwohiyudi iyuno dagohiyuni nugeyuhvsgvna, yigi, elohi nusdv nahnano tla yawana,ta hiyoliga, yigi, Dave Sanders tsigehv
segments.translation: The world won’t let them go. Not long ago I was talking to my boy. I said to him, “If you are in a dark place, and you turn on a flashlight, it will light up and overpower the dark.” I told him. It’s the same… it’s the same if you’re not Christian. He’s got them in the dark. But if he believes and uses God’s name, the Devil will move then. The Devil does not want to be in there. That’s when there’s room to really believe. If they are going to believe, if they want to give up the way the world is… I don’t know if you know him, Dave Sanders, that was.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I knew him.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: “Wait awhile,” ᏥᏚᏬᎮᎸ ᏣᎾ,Ꮧ Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᎠᎵ,ᏣᏙᎲᏍᎩ ᏭᏩᏛ.ᎰᎮᏢ “How about let’s just wait awhile,” ᎤᏓᏙᎮᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ Ꮭ ᏯᏩᎾ,Ꮤ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᏄᏮᏁᎸ ᎾᎮᎾ ᎣᏂ ᎢᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏭᏲᎱᏒ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏎ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᏄᏮᏁᎴ
segments.transliteration: “Wait awhile,” tsiduwohelv tsana,di gi.lo ali,tsadohvsgi wuwadv.hohetlv “How about let’s just wait awhile,” udadohelv tsadihv tla yawana,ta osda yinuwvnelv nahena oni iyusdi tsiwuyohusv squu ase osda yinuwvnele
segments.translation: “Wait awhile,” he told him. Some preacher came to see him. “How about let’s just wait awhile,” he told him. I don’t know if he became Christian and he died right after that. It would’ve been good if he did make it right.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: I used to be a preacher at Marble City Church.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.text: Ꭸ.Ꮃ ᏌᏭ Ꮎ Lime Plant ᏧᏃᏞ ᎥᎾ ᏧᎸᏫᏍᏓᏁᎲ ‘Ꮲ ᎠᏯ ᎠᎩᎷᏨ “‘ᏢᏴ ᏫᏓᎬᏯᏘᏂᏙᎵ ᏫᏓᏗᏴᏟ, ᎥᎾ” ᎠᏪᎮᎸ ᏃᏊ ᏌᏊ ᏳᏩᎦ,ᏓᏃ “ᏓᏕᏏᏧ ᏫᏓᏗᏴᏟ,Ꮝ?” ᎠᏪᎮᎸ “ᎥᎥ ᏫᏕᏓ,Ꮫ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᏙᏳ, ᎣᎦᏣᏅ ᎠᎦ,ᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩ ᏌᏊ ᎣᎩᏁᏥ ᏬᎩᏴᏢᏅ ᎣᎦᏦᏛ ᏬᎩᏴᏢ ᎠᏨᏍᏙ ᏙᏳ ... ‘ᏢᏃ ᏫᎨᎲ ᎤᎴᏫᏍᏔᏅ ᎤᏍᏚᏅ ᏚᏠᏒ ᏝᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎯᎢᏭ’Ᏼ ᎬᎪᏩᏛ.Ꮧ ᏱᎨᎮ ᎠᏬᏰᏂ ᏍᎩ ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎩ ᎨᎲ ... ᏍᎩ Ꮳ.Ꮧ ᎠᎾᏨᏍᏗ ᎠᏎᎪᎩᎢ ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎩ ᏱᏚ--ᏚᏨᏍᏔᏅᏃ ᎬᎪᏩ,Ꮫ.Ꮧ ᏍᎩ ᎮᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎧᏃᎮᏗ
segments.transliteration: ge.la sawu na Lime Plant tsunotle vna tsulvwisdanehv ‘tlv aya agilutsv “‘tlvyv widagvyatinidoli widadiyvtli, vna” awehelv noquu saquu yuwaga,dano “dadesitsu widadiyvtli,s?” awehelv “vv wideda,dv” tsiyohelv doyu, ogatsanv aga,sdayvhvsgi saquu oginetsi wogiyvtlvnv ogatsodv wogiyvtlv atsvsdo doyu ... ‘tlvno wigehv ulewistanv usdunv dutlosv tladv squu hiiwu’yv gvgowadv.di yigehe awoyeni sgi uli,sigi gehv ... sgi tsa.di anatsvsdi asegogii uli,sigi yidu--dutsvstanvno gvgowa,dv.di sgi hena yusdi kanohedi
segments.translation: There was one there that worked at the Lime Plant. He said, “Someday, I’m gonna take you and we will go in.” So one day he said, “Are we gonna go in?” “Yeah, we can go,” I told him. We all got in the car; my wife and one of the kids. We went in. In the car, we went in. The lights were bright. We kept going, then he stopped. He closed the light. The lights went out. You couldn’t even see this far from your hand it was that dark. Just like you’re saying. The light is overpowering the dark. When the lights come back on you can see. That’s what the Bible says.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᏍᎩᏛᎧ...ᏍᎩᏛᎧ...ᏄᏍᏛ ᏍᏊ ᎪᏪᎵ ᏙᎲ? ᎠᏥᏎᎬ--ᎠᏥᏎᎪᎦ ᎤᎵ,ᏏᎩ, ᎠᏗᏅ ᏍᏊ ᏙᎲ? ᏙᏳ...ᎾᎮᎾ ᏦᏍᏓᏓᏅᏟ Tony ᏣᏃᏎᎰ...ᏐᎢ ᎠᏯᏙ.ᎯᎯ...Ꭻ.Ꮼ “Let’s go visit,” ᎠᏬᎮᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ ᎠᎩᎶᎯᏍᏔᏅ ᎩᎳ ᎢᎪᎯᏓ ᏫᏥᏍᏓᏩᏛᏒ ... Ꮭ ᏯᏩᏅ,Ꮤ Barber’Ꮲ ᏱᏩᏂᎷᏣ, ᎥᎾ ᎦᏁᎸ ᏣᏗᎲ Randolf England ... “Boy, that’s what I was lookin’ for, ᎩᎶ ᎠᎩᏩ,Ꮫ.ᎰᎯᎲ” ᎠᏗᎲ ᏍᎩᎮᎾ ᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏈᏍᏗ ᎢᎦ ᎠᏁᎯ, ᏴᏫ, ᎨᎩᎦ,ᏘᏰ ᏙᎲ?
segments.transliteration: sgidvka...sgidvka...nusdv squu goweli dohv? atsisegv--atsisegoga uli,sigi, adinv squu dohv? doyu...nahena tsosdadanvtli Tony tsanoseho...soi ayado.hihi...gu.wo “Let’s go visit,” awohelv tsadihv agilohistanv gila igohida witsisdawadvsv ... tla yawanv,ta Barber’tlv yiwanilutsa, vna ganelv tsadihv Randolf England ... “Boy, that’s what I was lookin’ for, gilo agiwa,dv.hohihv” adihv sgihena yusdi tsiquisdi iga anehi, yvwi, gegiga,tiye dohv?
segments.translation: That’s how it’s written. It says, “The light is overpowering the dark.” Ain’t it? Really. My brother, Tony, they call him. A Deacon from Cherry said to me one day, “Let’s go visit people.” I followed him right away. I don’t know if we got to Barber, that’s where Randolf England lived. “Boy, that’s what I was lookin’ for. For somebody to come see me,” he said. There are a lot of people who are just waiting.

segments.speaker: charlie-shell
segments.translation: Really.

segments.speaker: jerry-scott
segments.text: ᎾᎯᏳ ᎤᏬᎯᏳᏅ ᏣᏗᎲ ... ᎨᏍᏗ’ᎡᎧ ᎠᏎ ᎠᎵ,ᏣᏙᎲᏍᎩ, ᏳᎵ,ᏍᏙᏗ ᏱᎩ, ᎤᏬᎯᏳᏗ ᏴᏫ, ᎥᏍᎩᏭᏂᎦ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏯ, ᎮᎾ,--ᎠᏯ, ᎮᎾ, ᏥᎩ, ᎣᏍᏓᏝᏅᏝ Ꮻ,ᎦᏅᎬ ᎤᎾ--ᎤᎾᏠᏲᎴᎸ ᎨᎲ ᎠᏭ ᎫᏐᎢ, ᏫᎦᏅᎬ ... ᎠᏪᏅᏒ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏍᏊ ᎠᏩᏓᏅ,Ꮫ ᎦᏳᎳ ᎠᏩᏅᏌ, ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎪᏍᏗ, “good news” ᏓᏥᏩ,ᏛᎯᏙᎵ, ᎾᏩᎵ,ᏍᏓᏁᎮ ... ᎠᏪᎾ ᎤᏩᏌᏭ ᏥᏄᏪᏒ ᎣᏍᏓᏝᏅᏝ “ᎦᎪ ᎣᏍᏓ ᏱᏓᏮᏓᏬᏣ?” ᎠᏪᎮᎸ “John ᎨᏍᏗᏛ ᏗᏓᏬᏍᏗ ᏱᏛᏣᏍᏕᎸᎯ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ “ᎰᎯᏳᏅ ᎮᎾ, ᏃᎮᎾ, ᏥᎩ, we’ll lead you into Christ,” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ... ᏂᎦᏓ ᎣᎩᏂᎶᏒ Ꮎ Ꭹ.Ꮆ Ꮎ ᏱᎪᎯᏳᎲᏍᏗ ᏣᏅᏔᏍ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎾ, ᎤᏪᏥ, ᎠᎨᏯ ᎦᏬᏂᏍᎬ ᏍᏊ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᏊ “Yeah, John,” ᎠᎪᎮᎸ “Just—just—uh” ᎡᏧᎳᏛᏃ ᏬᎩᏂᏬᏂᏒᏃ ... “ᏍᎩᏛ ᏂᎦᏓ Ꭼ.Ꮒ, ᎨᏒ ᏱᏂᏨᏁᎸ, ᎯᏍᎬᎾᎨᎲ ᏃᏊᏅ Ꮎ ‘ᏥᏍᎬᎾ’ Ᏹ.ᏲᎮᎳ, ᏥᏌ, ᎦᎶᏁᏓ, *y’know* ᏕᏣᏓᏂᎸᎦ ᎮᎾ Ꮭ ᎮᎾ--Ꮭ ᎮᎾ ᏁᎳᎦᏭ” ᏥᏲᎮᎸ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ Ꮎ Roman’s Road ᏫᏥᏯᏘᏅᏍᏔᏅ ᏣᎾ,ᏗᎰ ᏳᏍᏗ ᎢᎦᏓ ᎠᎾᎵ,ᏣᏙᎲᏍᎩ, ᏍᎩᏳᏍᏗ ᏥᏃᏎᎸ ᏣᏅ,ᏔᏍ Ꮎ ᏙᏳ, ᎤᏬᎯᏳᏅ ᎾᎯᏳ ... ᏝᏍᏊ *week later* ᏥᎨᎲ ᏧᏃᏴᏟᏢ ᎤᏲᎱᏒ ᏥᏛᏳᏛᏅ Ꮎ ᎤᏥ ᎤᏛᏅ Ꮎ ᎠᏂ--ᎤᏍᏓᏴᎲᏍᎩᏛ ᎠᏩᎵᎮᎵᏨᏭ ᎤᏩᏌ, ᏧᏓᏅ,ᏖᏢ ᎤᏬᎯᏳ,Ꮧ ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎮᎾ,...ᏍᏗᎩᏓ ᎮᎾ, Ꭱ... ᏂᎪᎯᎸ ᎡᏙᎮ ᎨᎲ *church* ᏙᏱᏭ ᏰᏙᎯ, ᎨᎲ ᏍᏗᎩᏛ Ꮎ ᏕᎦᎳᏐᎲ ᎨᎲ ᏙᏱ ᏗᏢᏭ ᎪᎱᏍᏗᏭ ᏄᏓᎴ ᏯᏂᏃᎮ Ꭹ.Ꮆ Ꮎ’Ꭱ ᎾᎯᏳ ᎢᎦᏓ Ꮎ ᏍᎩᎧ ᏥᏄᏍᏗ Ꭹ.Ꮆ... Ꭹ.Ꮆ ᏳᏅ,ᏔᏃ ᏛᏲᎱᏏᏒ ᎾᎯᏳ ᏱᎪᎯᏳᎲᎦ ᏍᎩ ᏍᏊ ᏴᏓ, ᎠᏎᏅᎧ ᏱᎦᏓ ᏥᏌ, ᎦᏛ ᎾᎥ “ᏍᏆᏅ,ᏓᏓ,” ᏣᎪᎮᎴ “ᎾᏞᎬ.Ꮽ ᏫᎬᎾ,ᏛᏁᏍᏗ,” ᏣᎪᏎᎴ ᏍᎩᎾᎾ
